    The NBA's hottest team resides in South Texas. After knocking off the Utah Jazz in Salt Lake City on Sunday night, the San Antonio Spurs enter a upcoming week riding a 12-game winning streak — the franchise's longest in more than a decade. Last season featured only two streaks longer than the Spurs' dominant dozen: a 16-game early-season jaunt by the Oklahoma City Thunder (which, as you might remember, these Spurs snapped in the NBA Cup semifinals) and a 13-game run by the Detroit Pistons … who, as luck would have it, will welcome the Spurs to the Motor City on Tuesday night.

    Industry observers note that when a team goes on a winning streak this long, there's plenty of credit to go around. Let's highlight 12 things worth knowing about the Spurs' stampede to the top of the Western Conference — one for each win in the streak! — starting with … I mean, come on, where else can you start?

    After the Latest York Knicks ended his phenomenal third season just short of a championship, Wembanyama entered the summer with a bitter taste in his mouth … and he seems to have entered the new campaign intent on washing it out by devouring everything in his path.

    Wembanyama enters Tuesday's action third in the NBA in scoring (a career-high 28.6 points per game) and fifth in rebounding (11.6 caroms a night) while, for the fourth straight season, leading the league in blocked shots (4.3 swats per contest). He hasn't forsaken the 3-point arc, but he's taking a higher share of his shots than ever directly at the rim, and he's converting them at a predictably elite rate, shooting 79.5% in the restricted area — tops among players to take at least 50 point-blank shots.

    Recent findings suggest that (Third on that list, by the way? Friggin' Dylan Harper. Don't worry: We'll get back to him.).

    Big Vic is averaging — averaging! — 4.64 dunks per game. That's nearly two more flushes per game than last season (2.78), which was already a career high. As tactics go, "Let's get the biggest guy as close to the basket as possible and let him just put the ball into it" seems like a pretty smart strategy, and the Spurs have been reaping the benefits of it, scoring a scorching 126.6 points per 100 non-garbage-time possessions in Wemby's minutes, according to Cleaning the Glass — a mark that would rank head-and-shoulders above the Los Angeles Lakers' league-leading rate of offensive efficiency thus far.

    In a recent development, when it comes to "season-opening heaters," most of the attention has gone to the man most responsible for that No. 1-ranked Lakers offense, Luka Dončić — and understandably so. It's worth noting, though, that the big fella is right now on pace to shatter the all-time record for player efficiency rating while leading the NBA in win shares, value over replacement player and total plus-minus; the Spurs have outscored opponents by 257 points in Wemby's 417 minutes, equivalent to a staggering 29.5 points-per-100.

    Watch Wembanyama on a nightly basis — not just the "did he just finger-roll from past the free-throw line?!?" highlights, but the possession after possession where he completely warps the opposition's defense and defangs its offense just by standing there — and you come away feeling like the 22-year-old's control of the game is, or at least can be, total.

    It has been revealed that "Opponents can't really put me in a situation where I can't answer," Wembanyama recently told reporters. "So now all I have to do is not beat myself.".

    For more than three weeks, he hasn't — and, in a related story, nobody's beaten the Spurs, either.

    All right, take it easy there, Thanos. (Not sure if you've heard, but it's all about Dr. Doom right now.).

    Industry observers note that generally speaking, if you're in the top 10 on both ends of the floor, you can consider yourself a contender; if you're in the top five on both ends, you're in the inner circle. San Antonio enters Tuesday's action ranked second in the NBA in points scored and allowed per possession, according to Cleaning the Glass.

    According to recent reports, where'd the Spurs finish last year, you might ask? Oh, I'm so glad you did. They were … third in points scored per possession, and third in points allowed per possession. If that was good enough to get them to the Finals, maybe bumping up to second both ways will be enough to get them to the top of the mountain this time?

    San Antonio has a point differential of +180 for the season — the 21st-highest total ever through the first 14 games of a campaign, according to Stathead. Of the 20 teams above these Spurs, 17 made at least the conference finals; eight of them won it all.

    Recent findings suggest that here's another: The Spurs are blitzing their opponents by 15.2 points per 100 non-garbage-time possessions thus far — the best net rating in the sport. Since the 2003-04 season, only four teams have finished a season outscoring the opposition by more than 12 points-per-100. All four of them — the 2007-08 Boston Celtics, 2014-15 and 2016-17 Golden State Warriors, and the 2024-25 Thunder — went on to win the NBA championship.

    Sources indicate that according to Jared Dubin's adjusted efficiency metrics at Last Night in Basketball, which measure how much better or worse a team's offense and defense were than the league's average unit in that season, the 2026-27 Spurs presently have a net rating 11.4 points-per-100 better than league average. That ranks third in Dubin's database, which goes all the way back to the ABA-NBA merger in 1976 — behind only Michael Jordan's 1995-96 Chicago Bulls (who won the title) … and this year's Boston Celtics, who (Monday's loss to the Orlando Magic notwithstanding) have been pretty awesome this year.

    According to recent reports, san Antonio's average margin of victory thus far is 12.86 points per game. Only one team has ever finished a full season higher: the '24-25 Thunder (+12.87) … who, again, won the title.

    According to Basketball-Reference's Simple Rating System — a metric "that takes into account average point differential and strength of schedule" — this year's Spurs are 12.75 points better than league average. That's on pace to be the highest SRS rating in Basketball-Reference's database, ahead of teams like the '24-25 Thunder, 1970-71 Milwaukee Bucks, '95-96 Bulls and 1971-72 Los Angeles Lakers — all of whom (say it with me) won the title.

    It's early, obviously, and 14 games is too small a sample to draw any definitive conclusions. This much, though, seems clear. If folks start digging into the historical record in search of points of comparison to what you're doing, and they keep coming up with teams that won the NBA championship? You're probably doing something right.

    The backcourt logjam that some pundits anticipated last season never really materialized in San Antonio. De'Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle started; rookie Harper mostly came off the bench; the trio shared the floor for just 25 minutes during the regular season and 44 minutes in the playoffs, and the Spurs made it all the way to the NBA Finals. Not actually a problem, right?

    It has been revealed that well, that seemed less likely to be the case this season, after Harper authored a breakout performance in his first postseason — and followed it up by making it pretty clear that he wasn't particularly interested in continuing to come off the bench. That led Spurs head coach Mitch Johnson to decide to open this season with all three of his high-octane guards in the starting five, backstopped by Wembanyama with Devin Vassell operating as an ostensible small-ball power forward. The early returns have been explosive:.

    In a recent development, the Spurs have hammered opponents by 110 points in 141 minutes with Fox, Castle and Harper sharing the floor this season, according to PBP Stats. They're scoring and defending at league-best rates in those minutes … and yes, a lot of that stems from the fact that Wembanyama has been out there for every single one of them. It's also working, though, because the guards are each finding ways to get in where they fit in.

    Sources indicate that they're flying up the court, with more than 23% of San Antonio's offensive possessions coming in transition in the three-guard lineup, and those units scoring at near-league-best levels on the break. Castle and Harper are almost exclusively taking shots at the rim or from beyond the arc in those minutes, getting to either catch-and-shoot or attack downhill after an initial action bends the defense.

    Sources indicate that fox and Castle, both questionable 3-point shooters, have both been knocking down well over 40% of their triples in these alignments. When the pick-your-poison wheel spins to a center guarding Castle, the Spurs have shown their work in developing counters to that scheme.

    According to recent reports, and while conventional wisdom would warn you against the defensive drawbacks of playing small, with no player listed taller than 6-foot-6 at the 1 through 4 spots, those lineups have rebounded fine, haven't given up a ton of opportunities at the rim, and have yet to be significantly exploited for their lack of size on the perimeter. (It seems that having that French dude back there goes a long way toward bucking conventional wisdom.).

    "I understand the narrative around it. I always land on the same reasoning at the very end of it," Johnson told reporters about starting the three guards during the preseason. "They're three of our better players. [...] I think they can dribble, pass, shoot, defend, make winning plays.".

    According to recent reports, whether they'll continue to do so in this alignment remains to be seen; when offseason signing/veteran power forward Tobias Harris heals up from the calf injury that has cost him the opening month of the season, Johnson will likely have a difficult decision to make. Then again, if the not-so-small-ball Spurs keep blowing everybody's doors off in this look … maybe he won't.

    Sources indicate that "The biggest thing is, I've got handlers all around me — guys that we want to put the ball in their hands and pick-and-roll around me," Wembanyama said. "That makes things easier.".

    Why mess with easier, you know?

    Since opening the season with losses to the Thunder and Rockets, the Spurs have gotten the opportunity to get right with a pretty friendly stretch of road.

    According to recent reports, they've had three games against the Jazz, two games against the Kings, and matchups with the Suns and Bulls. They've also caught the Timberwolves without Anthony Edwards or Rudy Gobert, the Mavericks without Cooper Flagg or Kyrie Irving, the Trail Blazers without Ja Morant, and the Warriors right after Stephen Curry went down.

    Industry observers note that add it all up, and the Spurs' season-opening slate ranks among the softest in the NBA, according to multiple strength-of-schedule metrics. San Antonio doesn't have to apologize for that, of course. You play the teams that are in front of you, with whoever's in uniform for them when you show up. We've seen plenty of teams fail to capitalize on the opportunity to take down a team at less than full strength. (Looking at you, Mavs.).

    Besides, when presented with matchups against shorthanded or sorry opposition, the Spurs have done what good teams are supposed to do: namely, win all of those games, with most of those victories coming by double digits. It's just something to keep an eye on, particularly with a tough opponent like Detroit up next … before three more against the Clippers, Pelicans and Kings. (The games to really keep an eye on? November 27 against Luka and the Lakers, and November 29 against that damn good Celtics team.).

    According to recent reports, fox got raked over the coals this summer for his underperformance in the NBA Finals. (Which, it's worth remembering, came with him nursing a high ankle sprain that likely would've sidelined him for weeks had it been the regular season.) His struggles under the brightest lights, combined with Harper's stellar showing in his maiden postseason voyage, primed the pump for the shift to the three-guard lineup, and led to no shortage of calls for the veteran triggerman to cede the stage — and his spot in the Spurs' pecking order — to the rising sophomore.

    Well, Fox is still here … and he's kind of threading the needle.

    Fox has taken a clear step back in the Spurs' offensive hierarchy, averaging fewer minutes and points per game than he has since his rookie season, and posting far and away the lowest usage rate, time of possession and average number of touches of his 10-year career. He's taking seven fewer field goal attempts per 100 possessions than he did last year.

    When Fox shares the floor with Harper and Castle, he's finishing just 15.7% of San Antonio's offensive possessions with a shot attempt, foul drawn or turnover — the kind of usage rate more commonly associated with a complementary player like Isaiah Hartenstein, Toumani Camara or Christian Braun than with a two-time All-Star who has averaged 21 points per game in his career. He's performing well in that reduced role, though.

    Fox more frequently takes high-percentage shots — 32% of his attempts are coming at the rim, his highest rate in six years, while corner 3s account for 12% of his shots, a career high — and has almost totally excised long 2-pointers from his repertoire. That, in turn, has led to more efficient scoring. He enters Tuesday's action toting a .551 effective field goal percentage (which accounts for 3-pointers being worth more than 2-pointers) and a .621 true shooting percentage (which factors in 2-point, 3-point and free-throw accuracy) — both of which are by far the highest marks of his career.

    He has paired that leaner shot diet with a voracious appetite for freebies, too drawing shooting fouls on more than 19% of his field-goal attempts — again, a career high. In fact, among 153 players who have logged at least 300 minutes this season, Fox's .496 free-throw attempt rate is the 11th-highest in the NBA, just ahead of free-throw-magnet massive men Joel Embiid and Giannis Antetokounmpo.

    Sources indicate that pair that just-the-facts-ma'am scoring game with his ongoing facilitation — a team-high 5.8 assists per game, including 33 to Wemby, making them the third-most-frequent assist combo in the NBA thus far — and Fox has managed to continue providing value while still making room for the evolution of the young talent around him. Not bad.

    Industry observers note that for fans of a certain age, thinking of the Spurs might evoke images of patient, methodical offensive possessions — all entry passes to Tim Duncan on the low block or swing-swing symphonies of "good-to-great" ball movement, where the pace of their play is secondary to the precision of their movements. These aren't your daddy's Spurs, though; these dudes have a predilection toward moving fast and breaking things. Like, for example, you.

    It has been revealed that in terms of overall pace of play, the Spurs rank just 24th in the NBA, with their average game featuring about 98.8 possessions, according to NBA Advanced Stats. That's due in large part to their defense, though; San Antonio has the longest average defensive possession in the NBA this season, according to PBP Stats. That stands to reason: When you've got to try to figure out how to crowbar open a crevice to attack with Wembanyama menacing along the back line while the likes of Castle and Harper pressure the ball up top, it might take you a little while.

    Once the Spurs get the ball, though, they hit the gas. San Antonio has the fifth-fastest average offensive possession this season, and is tied for the fifth-quickest average time to shot, according to Inpredictable.

    As noted by the great John Schuhmann, the Spurs lead the NBA in both transition points scored and allowed per game, outscoring opponents by 13 points a night on the break — a massive gap. With their ability to force turnovers, finish possessions with rebounds and advance the ball to all those jet-fueled guards, more than 19% of their offensive possessions come in transition, according to Cleaning the Glass; that's the most in the league. But thanks to their ability to protect the defensive glass, take care of the ball and sprint back, fewer than 12% of their defensive possessions come in transition … which is also No. 1 in the league.

    Since at least the start of the 2003-04 season, no team has ever finished the year No. 1 in the league at both generating and preventing transition opportunities. Just another way these Spurs are on pace (ha!) to dispense with conventional wisdom.

    Winning the possession battle isn't exactly a revolutionary concept; coaches have been preaching since time immemorial the importance of taking care of the ball on offense and finishing possessions on defense. It's become an increasingly large point of emphasis in recent years, though, as front offices and coaching staffs engaged in the perpetual pursuit of optimization, hunting for every advantage on both ends of the floor. As it turns out, "making sure we get more chances to shoot and score than the other guys" is a pretty solid way to approach things!

    The Spurs were pretty good at that last season. When you factor in how many offensive rebounds they pulled in against how many they gave up, how many free-throw attempts they racked up versus how many they conceded, and how many times they turned the ball over compared with how many times they forced opponents to cough it up, San Antonio generated 2.2 more offensive possessions than its opponents per game during the regular season — a good number, but not quite in the upper echelons of the league, like the team that knocked them off in the Finals.

    This season, though, the Spurs have tightened the screws virtually across the board. They're grabbing an even higher share of their own missed shots, turning the ball over at the NBA's lowest rate and getting to the free-throw line more frequently, while also forcing more turnovers and curbing their foul rate. Add it up, and through 14 games, San Antonio is generating 7.2 more possessions per game than its opponents — a massive leap over last season, and the No. 1 mark in the league thus far.

    Sources indicate that make sure you take more shots on goal than the other guys and you've got a great shot at winning a lot more often than you lose — especially when you put the ball in the hands of dudes who can make those shots. Dudes like ….

    … the 20-year-old sophomore, whose combination of throwback cool and downhill explosiveness just keeps leaping off the screen pretty much every time you see him.

    Harper has responded to his elevation into the starting lineup by continuing to ball out. His usage, free-throw attempt rate and scoring efficiency are all up; his turnover rate is down. Some of that, obviously, comes from more frequently sharing the floor with multiple other high-level ball-handlers, but still: pretty nice to have the guy who's second on your team in touches only coughing it up 8% of the time, one of the lowest rates of any guard in the league.

    According to recent reports, coming off that sensational rookie season, Harper is pretty firmly establishing himself as one of the best players in the league when it comes to getting into the paint and finishing on the interior, shooting a frankly bananas 78.6% in the restricted area — better than high-efficiency bigs like Domantas Sabonis, Jarrett Allen, Walker Kessler and Giannis Antetokounmpo. Decent company for a 6-foot-5 sophomore.

    According to recent reports, through 14 games, Harper is averaging 18.3 points, 5.5 rebounds, 4.7 assists and 1.0 steals in 31.5 minutes per game, shooting 55% inside the arc, 34% from long distance and 87% from the charity stripe. The list of players to average 18-4-4 for a full season by their age-20 season is just six names long: Magic Johnson, LeBron James, Tyreke Evans, Dončić, LaMelo Ball and Cooper Flagg. Of that group, only Magic shot at least 50% from the field, as Harper is right now.

    There's a 7-foot-4 caveat to that, of course. With the exception of rookie Magic playing alongside MVP Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, those other preternatural playmakers didn't have a gravitational force like Wemby pulling attention away from them and opening up opportunities to slash, score and create. But opportunities only matter insofar as you can capitalize on them, and Harper continues to make the most out of his privileged position, perpetually pressuring the defense and looking for all the world like an All-Star in the making — sooner rather than later.

    It's not all beer and Skittles in San Antonio, though. As lights-out as the newly introduced-look starting lineup has been, moving Harper into the first five has led to some predictable ripple effects in the second unit. The Spurs' reserve corps has a negative net rating for the season, and has — as you might expect — been significantly worse in the minutes when Luke Kornet checks in for Wembanyama, struggling to score even with at least one of Fox, Castle or Harper on the floor.

    Industry observers note that some of those struggles might be mitigated by the introduction of Harris, whom the Spurs signed to a two-year, $31 million contract in free agency, and who's yet to play after suffering a left calf strain during training camp. But Johnson will have to shuffle his rotation to make space for the veteran forward. What impact might that have on the minutes and productivity of the likes of Julian Champagnie, whose quick-trigger 3-point shooting has proven so vital for this iteration of the Spurs? Or Keldon Johnson, the reigning Sixth Man of the Year? Or Harrison Barnes, one of just two Spurs (along with Champagnie) knocking down at least 40% of his triples? Or second-year power forward Carter Bryant, whose ongoing development is a clear priority for San Antonio's future aims?

    It has been revealed that if Harris isn't able to hit the ground running — specifically by spacing the floor at a high level, as he did for Cade Cunningham in Detroit last season — it could throw some sand into the gears of a Spurs offense that has been humming despite not generating a ton from beyond the arc. San Antonio ranks just 26th in the league in the share of its shots that come from beyond the arc, and right around league-average in 3-point shooting accuracy.

    Industry observers note that that lagging 3-point attempt rate clearly hasn't hampered the offense's effectiveness thus far; some of it stems from the fact that the Spurs hammer the rim as frequently and effectively as nearly any team in the league. After finishing above league-average in 3-point attempt rate the last three seasons, though, you'd imagine Johnson would prefer to find ways to get a few more up — if for no other reason than to be prepared to have multiple styles to play when the postseason comes around and defensive game looks prioritize clogging the paint to take away Wembanyama's rolls to the rim and the three-headed guard monster's driving lanes to the basket.

    If opposing defenses are able to congest the interior and force the Spurs to sing for their supper from outside, it'll bring to the forefront perhaps the most significant matter carrying over from last season: whether they have enough bankable 3-point shooting.

    In a recent development, as it stands, the entire starting five — Wembanyama, Fox, Castle, Harper and Vassell — currently sits below 35% from deep for the season. Reigning Sixth Man of the Year Johnson is at 22.7%; erstwhile unicorn-turned-indoor cat Kornet hasn't attempted a long ball since April of 2025. The Spurs can make a lot of magic happen in tight confines, thanks to the size and brilliance of Wembanyama, and the speed, skill and force of their guards. If hardly anybody in the rotation can make a jumper when they need to, though, problems will arise.

    It has been revealed that those issues — the bench minutes, the shooting, etc. — are not exactly surprises to the Spurs. They're well aware that they've got room to improve.

    "If we felt like we're the best version of ourselves at this point in the season, we'll be in trouble," Keldon Johnson recently told reporters.

    It has been revealed that as excellent as their offense has been, the Spurs have actually underperformed their expected shot quality by the league's fifth-largest amount, according to Synergy Sports Technology's tracking — and all four teams above them in that ranking (Charlotte, Milwaukee, Utah, Chicago) have been terrible, without the talent to meaningfully bridge the gap between expectation and reality. That's certainly not the case in San Antonio.

    If Wembanyama (35% from deep last season, 32% this season), Vassell (38% last season, 31% this season) and Johnson (36% last season, 23% this season) tick up toward their previous marks, and any of Fox, Harper or Castle nudge up toward league-average on their looks, this Spurs offense might have another level to reach. Honestly, it might even if only one of those guys keeps the arrow pointed north. You can probably guess which one.

    It has been revealed that "I can still do more," Wembanyama told reporters after his 52-point masterpiece against the Mavericks. "I mean, my shots weren't falling tonight and that forces me into a style of play that is exhausting. I can do it. I mean, the proof is here. I can do it, but I can be much better if my shots fall. I know it's just a matter of time.".

    If that happens — if the shots start to fall, the offense soars and the defense remains elite — then it might just be a matter of time before the Spurs are hoisting the Larry O'Brien Championship Trophy, too.

    Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

    There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

    Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

    You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

    In a recent development, it was a shame because in that cameo, Fernandes highlighted he has returned from the World Cup in excellent shape, the tempo of United’s play immediately lifting when he had the ball. It is wrong to make conclusions in the summer, but you are on safe ground to state he will be integral to their ambitions.

    Croke Park is a stadium steeped in history and another chapter was penned here, as the capacity crowd made this the highest attended soccer match in Ireland with 82,000 coming through the gates: it is a magnificent venue, one that would be well capable of hosting a Champions League final.

    Michael Carrick hopes in years to come that is the stage where his team will be but, right now, it is a case of learning to walk again before they can run and he more than anyone will know how far off that target is, not that it will stop him trying to get there.

    The one thing that is obvious about the way United play under him is the first thought from everyone is to go forward promptly. Yes, this was only a friendly, but the ambition to be on the front foot and cause problems was evident from the start.

    The team in red had much the better of the opening exchanges, with Diogo Dalot having the first shot that went over but, unlike on July 25, when Mayo beat Kerry here in Gaelic football’s All Ireland final, which went viral, nobody was cheering the sight of a ball clearing the bar.

    It was like a home game for United and the majority got what they wanted in the 15th minute when a slick counter-attack ended with Bryan Mbuemo sliding a pass into Joshua Zikzee, who rifled past James Trafford with a first-time finish.

    Sources indicate that devastating counterattack! 💥Manchester United break and Joshua Zirkzee is there to finish it off 🤩 pic.twitter.com/y6QHbZMi7n.

    Zirkzee is unlikely to be part of Carrick’s squad beyond the transfer window, with interest from clubs in Italy, and it would be disingenuous to suggest his career at Old Trafford has been successful, but his attitude was exemplary and he played as if he was desperate to change his manager’s mind.

    There may have been an anticipation that United would stride clear, but this game was also about Leeds, whose summer has been encouraging and whose confidence from staying up last season has evidently enabled them to blossom.

    Sources indicate that you would be way off the mark if you include them in your conversations about which clubs are going to be relegated next May, and the sense they revealed to stay with Daniel Farke has paid off. They have bought some good players, not least goalkeeper James Trafford and Harry Wilson.

    In a recent development, top stop from James Trafford! 🚫The Leeds United keeper has been busy in the first half... pic.twitter.com/VKmxNVKBsA.

    In a recent development, trafford has done the right thing getting away from Manchester City and you could argue that he is already reaping the benefit of playing for a manager who wants him, as he made a fabulous save in the 23rd minute to thwart Mbuemo. It was all part of performance that led to him being named player of the match.

    He was involved in the move that brought the Leeds equaliser, too, as his long clearance caused uncertainty and led to Tyler Fletcher being pickpocketed by Dan James and he nudged a pass into Brenden Aaronson, who kept his cool and danced into the area, ignoring Senne Lammens, to finish.

    According to recent reports, leeds hit back with their first shot on target! 💥Brenden Aaronson with a cool finish 🥶 pic.twitter.com/5WsSZY41j6.

    Recent findings suggest that it was an entertaining affair, mercifully lacking the bile that would usually bubble away when it is staged in England, and the longer the game advanced, the better Leeds looked. They finished the opening period strongly and came back after the restart, with 10 changes, in the same fettle.

    Farke, whose team had shown their ability to score heavily when they pummelled Liverpool 4-2 in Chicago 10 days ago, would have taken plenty of encouragement, but the perfectionist in him would have cursed the opportunities that were squandered early in the second period.

    Industry observers note that the misses proved costly as the game meandered and the shoot-out went United’s way, after Wilson and James Justin failed from 12 yards, with Noussair Mazraoui thumping in the decisive kick. It really is never dull.

    Manchester United Lammens (Mee 61); Dalot (Mazraoui 60), Yoro, Heaven (Armer 46), Amass (Shaw 60); Santos (Collyer 46), T Fletcher (Tielemans 61); Diallo (J Fletcher 60), Zirkzee (Cunha 60), Dorgu (Thompson 46); Mbuemo (Fernandes 60).Subs not used Heath, Honor, Lacey, Gabriel.

    Leeds United Trafford (Cairns 46); Bijol (Rodon 46), Muharemovic (Cresswell 46), Bornauw; Bogle (Gnonto 46), Longstaff (Stach 46), Tanaka (Ampadu 46), Chadwick (Justin 46); James (Okafor 46), Aaronson (Wilson 46); Nmecha (Calvert-Lewin 46).Subs not used Mahady, Lienou, Mills, Piroe.

    Sources indicate that decent enough watch for roughly half the game, settled on a shoot-out in which Alex Cairns got nowhere near any of Manchester United’s penalties. Doubt he will lose much sleep over it. Bruno Fernandes grinned broadly when he missed.

    Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the pre-season friendly between Manchester United and Leeds United at a sold-out Croke Park in Dublin. Last year Leeds played Milan in the Irish capital and drew a crowd of 52,000 but at the GAA citadel, as I think I’m contractually obliged to call it, there will be 83,000 present, a testament to the Premier League’s reach and these two clubs’ popularity in Ireland founded on the exploits of Billy Whelan, Noel Cantwell, Johnny Giles, Roy Keane, Gary Kelly et al. It’s the first club match ever held at the stadium.

    It’s a fixture that always stirs the blood and whenever it comes around you can guarantee that there will be reams of stuff about the War of the Roses, clash in styles, Busby and Revie, Bobby and Jack, large swathes of which this author has been guilty of producing. I’ll spare you all that today because while it’s relevant to fans of both clubs, they know it backwards. And it’s a match that has come around a wee bit too frequently in pre-season recently, first in Perth, Western Australia, in 2019 when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s side beat Marcelo Bielsa’s 4-0, then in 2023 in Oslo when Erik ten Haag’s second or third string defeated Daniel Farke’s threadbare, just relegated squad 2-0 and last year in Stockholm, which ended in a 0-0 draw between two scratch sides.

    Sources indicate that this one comes round later in the pre-season schedule than those three so we can expect to see stronger XIs, at least for part of the game. Leeds’ pre-season has gone well: after a 3-2 defeat by Wrexham in Tampa, they have beaten Sunderland in New Jersey, Liverpool in Chicago and RB Leipzig at Elland Road. Manchester United also lost to Wrexham (in Helsinki) then beat Rosenborg in Trondheim, Atlético in Stockholm and drew one apiece with the European champions, PSG, in Gothenburg last time out.

    While Leeds will have latest signing James Trafford available and Noah Okafor, who scored twice in Leeds’ first league victory at Old Trafford for 45 years last April, in the squad for the first time after the World Cup, Manchester United have Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford back in training since the start of the week but it seems too soon for them to start but Youri Tielemans is pushing to make his first start.

    • Fresh York Yankees ace Cam Schlittler is the winner of the American League Cy Young Award for 2026.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Fresh York Yankees ace Cam Schlittler is the winner of the American League Cy Young Award for 2026. Schlittler was a unanimous selection via the Baseball Writers Association of America balloting, the results of which were announced on Wednesday, beating out Blue Jays ace Dylan Cease and Guardians rookie Parker Messick.

    Schlittler's win snapped the run of free agent Tarik Skubal, who won the last two AL Cy Youngs as a member of the Detroit Tigers.

    This past season, the right-handed Schlitter in his age-25 campaign put up dominant numbers:.

    According to recent reports, in addition to the above, Schlitter led AL pitchers in WAR with a mark of 7.0, and his ERA+ of 215 also paced his league. That 215 ERA+, which means that Schlittler's park-adjusted ERA was 115% better than the league average, is a Yankees franchise record. Among Yankee qualifiers, only Ron Guidry's 208 in 1978 comes close. Additionally, Schlittler tied for the AL lead this season with an FIP of 2.56, and he struck out 31.4% of opposing batters, which also ranked second in the AL.

    Without Schlittler's top-shelf contributions, the Yankees, without franchise slugger and reigning back-to-back AL MVP Aaron Judge for almost 100 games, might have struggled to make the postseason. Instead, Schlittler's excellence at the front of the rotation helped them win 93 games, post the AL's top run differential, and advance to the ALDS.

    Recent findings suggest that "Cam had as dominant a season as a starting pitcher can have from start to finish," Yankees manager Aaron Boone said in a statement. "He's shown an astonishing amount of growth since we drafted him, and his success is no accident. Cam has a tireless appetite for hard work and refinement that has allowed his talents to truly flourish. This Cy Young is richly deserved. Cam was the most dominant pitcher in our league and continues to grow into a foundational player for this franchise.".

    While Schlittler was outstanding as a rookie in 2025, this past season, he increased usage of his sinker and cutter and improved ride on his 98-mph fastball helped him take the next step and become one of the very pitchers in all of baseball. Since Schlittler doesn't turn 26 until February, continued dominance may be on the way.

    Sources indicate that schlittler is now the seventh Yankee to win the Cy Young Award. He joins teammate Gerrit Cole in 2023, Roger Clemens in 2001, Guidry in 1978, Sparky Lyle in 1977, Whitey Ford in 1961, and Bob Turley in 1958.

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that fill in your charts, Scorigami fans: We have yet another score that had never happened before in 107 years of NFL history.
    • It took some oddities and some late-game madness to get there, as is pretty much always the case when looking for a unique score.
    • SF 46 - DAL 40🚨 SCORIGAMI 🚨That is the 1099th unique score in NFL history, and the 4th of the 2026 season.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that fill in your charts, Scorigami fans: We have yet another score that had never happened before in 107 years of NFL history. The 49ers' 46-40 win over the Cowboys is the first 46-40 game on record.

    It took some oddities and some late-game madness to get there, as is pretty much always the case when looking for a unique score. There were five touchdowns, a failed two-point conversion and two successful two-point conversions in the fourth quarter alone!

    SF 46 - DAL 40🚨 SCORIGAMI 🚨That is the 1099th unique score in NFL history, and the 4th of the 2026 season. pic.twitter.com/qW3tfAiLSJ.

    Recent findings suggest that entering the fourth quarter, the 49ers led 31-19, not a super common score, but nothing too absurd: That score has happened 17 times before. A missed Brandon Aubrey extra point earlier in the game created the strange number for Dallas.

    According to recent reports, then all hell (or, for Scorigami fans, heaven) broke loose. Christian McCaffrey scored on a 16-yard run. Dallas answered with a long touchdown drive but failed on the two-point conversion. At 38-25, the scoring chances rose. As a general rule, as the score rises astronomically, so, too, do the chances for a unique score. The Cowboys got a stop and scored again, this time kicking the extra point to make it 38-32. That score has happened before, albeit only three times.

    According to recent reports, it took just two plays for the 49ers to find the end zone, with Brock Purdy finding McCaffrey jetting off for a 66-yard touchdown. Purdy also found McCaffrey for the two-point conversion. That was major, because 44-32 and 45-32 have both happened before (once each). But 46-32 had never happened before.

    According to recent reports, luckily, one final Dak Prescott touchdown pass and, crucially, a successful two-point conversion didn't ruin things, either. The two-point conversion was actually crucial, because 46-38 has happened before. So, everyone, please applaud Dak Prescott's effort here.

    Dak converts the two-point conversion!We've got a six-point game 👀SFvsDAL on FOX/FOX OneStream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/SjVjt43GD9.

    According to recent reports, the next Scorigami will be the 1,100th unique score in NFL history, and hopefully, it will be half as fun as this game was. This was also the fourth Scorigami this season, a rare feat in itself.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    You can't make the playoffs in 10 games, but you can definitely give yourself some breathing room when the inevitable ebbs and flows of the season strike. That's exactly what the Boston Bruins have done as they've stood out for the right reasons in a deep Atlantic Division.

    Boston at the moment leads the division with 15 points, and while the Tampa Bay Lightning's record is technically better, the Bruins' plus-14 goal differential is tied for second in the NHL.

    The biggest reason for this fast start has been the play of Jeremy Swayman in goal. He's allowed one or fewer goals in half of his starts, and Swayman's 8.02 goals saved above average ranks second to old Beantown running mate Linus Ullmark, per Natural Stat Trick.

    We have a long way to go before we start discussing Vezina Trophy candidates seriously, but Swayman certainly has the potential to carry Boston to the postseason.

    According to recent reports, it helps that David Pastrnak is an elite playmaker, and the Bruins have been getting contributions from young forwards Fraser Minten and James Hagens. Morgan Geekie has also gone from goal-scoring machine to distributor with seven assists in 10 games.

    Sources indicate that the Atlantic Division will be a heavyweight brawl throughout the season, but to this point, the Bruins have proven to be a worthy combatant. With that in mind, here are the updated NHL Power Rankings.

    #15559. Tech Report: National League Reliever of the Year: Matt Snyder explains his 2026 BBWAA ballot

    📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1014 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: National League Reliever of the Year: Matt Snyder explains his 2026 BBWAA ballot

    📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1014 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, mason Miller of the Padres won the 2026 National League Reliever of the Year award on Wednesday evening.
    • First off, I didn't even bother to look at win-loss record.
    • Sources indicate that what makes the best relievers?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, mason Miller of the Padres won the 2026 National League Reliever of the Year award on Wednesday evening. That wasn't all too surprising, but I still wanted to explain the thought process behind my ballot. This was an honor, as it was the first-ever Baseball Writers' Association of America award for a relief pitcher. Yes, there have been plenty of reliever awards over the years, but this was the first year the BBWAA handed out such hardware.

    1. Mason Miller, Padres2. Jhoan Duran, Phillies3. Adrián Morejón, Padres4. Trevor Megill, Brewers5. Mason Montgomery, Pirates.

    And now here's how it unfolded on my end.

    First off, I didn't even bother to look at win-loss record. It's a flawed enough stat these days with any individual player, but we really shouldn't be judging relievers by it. I'm also not worried about team performance here, as this is an individual award and we don't even need to wrestle with the word "valuable" being in the title like some MVP voters might. This is simply, "Who was the best relief pitcher in the league?".

    Sources indicate that what makes the best relievers? Run prevention (ERA, FIP, xFIP, etc.) matters, as does keeping runners off base (WHIP). It's helpful not only to the defense to strike hitters out, but it can also help a reliever bail out his team, so that's going to matter. Workload matters as well, as a reliever eating up as many outs as possible is very valuable to a team. I didn't factor saves as much as keeping leads (blown saves can hurt). Something I find helpful in judging relievers is win probability added. A reliever blowing games is going to be dinged in a significant way, while closing down tougher games (one-run leads as opposed to three) is going to score extra via this measure. It's trickier with relievers, but WAR can help tell a story here, too.

    According to recent reports, finally, I have no doubt there was some eye test involved. That is, when I'm watching a game, which reliever coming out of the bullpen feels the most imposing to the opposition. Miller, Duran and Megill especially got bonus points here.

    A quick rundown of the major stats I examined follows.

    Among NL relievers, Miller was the best in ERA (1.67), xERA, FIP, xFIP and several other categories. Duran was second in ERA (and xERA, FIP and xFIP) with Yuki Matsui third, Brandyn Garcia fourth and Abner Uribe fifth. Megill was third in FIP, while Montgomery was third in xFIP and Morejón was fourth.

    In terms of keeping runners off base, Garcia led NL relievers in WHIP; Megill was second, Miller third, Duran ninth and Montgomery 10th.

    Kudos to Garcia for the excellent season, but his workload (51 ⅓ innings) dinged him a bit. Speaking of, Morejón worked 86 innings compared to 70 from Miller, 63 ⅔ from Montgomery, 61 ⅔ from Megill and 59 ⅓ from Duran.

    That remarked, Garcia, Matsui and Uribe are firmly in the mix through these categories.

    It has been revealed that miller crushes here. He struck out 129 hitters, giving him 16.6 K/9 and a 47.4 K%. Montgomery was second in strikeout rate at 37.7%. Yes, it was that much of a blowout for Miller. Duran was third at 35.6%. Garcia was sixth, Morejón ninth, Megill 14th, Uribe 25th and Matsui 28th.

    Miller tied for the league lead in saves with Riley O'Brien. I never considered O'Brien, as his ERA was north of 4.00.

    In a recent development, miller was also 38 of 41 in save chances. Duran was 33 of 35. Megill had 30 saves and seven holds with only three blown saves. Montgomery had 18 saves and nine holds with three blown saves. Morejón blew five saves, but he had three saves and 28 holds with an awful lot of multi-inning appearances. Uribe had six saves and 23 holds with two blown saves. Garcia? Stellar. He closed down five saves and 18 holds without ever blowing a lead. Matsui never blew a lead either, but he only had one save and 10 holds, meaning he wasn't tasked with much in the way of high-leverage innings. Being teammates with Miller and Morejón (and Jasaon Adam and Bradgley Rodríguez) will do that. As such, along with his relatively low strikeout rate, we can safely eliminate Matsui.

    By the time I've gotten here, I have seven players for five spots: Miller, Morejón, Duran, Megill, Montgomery, Uribe and Garcia.

    Using the FanGraphs calculation, Miller leads the way by a country mile at 3.7. Duran is second at 2.9, with Morejón at 2.8 and Megill at 2.5. Montgomery is eighth, Uribe ninth and Garcia, due in part to the workload concern, down at 17th.

    In a recent development, over on Baseball Reference's version, Duran actually leads the way at 3.4. Miller is next at 3.1, followed by Montgomery (2.4) and Uribe (2.3). Megill sits at 1.7 while both Morejón and Garcia are at 1.9.

    Industry observers note that in WPA, yes, Miller leads the way again at 4.56. Uribe is second at 3.49, with Morejón third at 3.23, Montgomery fourth at 2.86, Megill seventh, Garcia eighth and Duran 11th.

    Miller in first place wasn't all too difficult. He was the best relief pitcher in baseball in 2026 and checked every single box.

    I had trouble with Duran over Morejón, while Megill and Montgomery were also very close in that group, as were Uribe and Garcia. I ended up leaning on Duran's high strikeout rate and excellent run prevention, which helped clear the way for his lead in WAR. Morejón's workload meant I couldn't go any lower than third with him, given how many crucial outs he soaked up for the Padres. Megill's regular-season numbers were better than Uribe's, notably the under-the-hood numbers, even if they were very close. And Montgomery was an absolute beast for the Pirates.

    It was incredibly tough to leave Uribe off, and Garcia was my hard-luck seventh-place finisher here when I had only five spots on my ballot.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In lockstep with Week 10 kicking off, the second half of the regular season is underway.
    • Even with seven weeks left to go in the regular season, I'm ready to call two awards right now:.
    • What we saw from both of them in Week 10 only bolsters their case, if not outright putting the final nail in the coffin to eventually go home with the awards when we get to the NFL Honors during Super Bowl week.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In lockstep with Week 10 kicking off, the second half of the regular season is underway. Naturally, there's going to be plenty of twists and turns as we barrel down the stretch run. Teams will jockey for playoff positioning while players and coaches look to put themselves in contention for awards such as MVP, Defensive Player of the Year and more. When it comes to awards, two are already in the bag.

    Even with seven weeks left to go in the regular season, I'm ready to call two awards right now:.

    What we saw from both of them in Week 10 only bolsters their case, if not outright putting the final nail in the coffin to eventually go home with the awards when we get to the NFL Honors during Super Bowl week.

    Sources indicate that when it comes to Monken, who opened at +1400 to win the award at DraftKings Sportsbook, he has remarkably put the Browns in the AFC playoff picture after jumping out to a 6-4 record. That record includes a 4-0 mark at home, the first time the franchise has done so since 1963.

    He's also coached through some tightly contested games. In fact, Monken's Browns are the first team in NFL history to have their first six wins each come by four points or less. To his credit, Monken named Deshaun Watson the starter this summer, which is a move that has borne fruit. Watson has been solid this season, notching six game-winning drives. He's also thrown for at least 300 yards in each of his past three games, making him just the third Browns quarterback to do so.

    Sunday's win over the Texans also inched Cleveland closer to securing a playoff spot. Even as they entered Week 10 with a 3-5 record, Houston was a dark horse to possibly oust the Browns from a playoff spot. However, after knocking them down to 3-6 and claiming the head-to-head tiebreaker, they've largely killed that possibility in its crib.

    BROWNS WIN pic.twitter.com/mQGRiqo4mM.

    Moreover, when you look at the rest of the competition in the wild card race, there's not much to speak of.

    The Ravens (4-5 before Monday night) are starting a backup after Lamar Jackson went down with a fractured right thumb. Meanwhile, the Patriots (5-5) could be starting a backup for the foreseeable future depending on the severity of Drake Maye's ankle injury. Then, you have the Raiders, who are 4-6 and are working in a rookie quarterback. The Browns host Las Vegas in Week 12 following their bye week, putting themselves in a strong position to pick up yet another key head-to-head tiebreaker.

    In a recent development, the path is quite clear for them to secure a wild card spot. If/when that happens, Monken is the runaway favorite for Coach of the Year. Right now, he's +370 at DraftKings Sportsbook, tied with John Harbaugh for the second-best odds, as they both look up to Kyle Shanahan (+300). The smart money should be on Monken.

    Industry observers note that as for Mahomes, he was the favorite to win Comeback Player of the Year from the jump, but was still +185 to win it at the start of the season. While they were short odds at the time, getting it at plus money feels like stealing right now.

    After suffering a torn ACL and LCL last season, Mahomes has come back and helped Kansas City to a 7-2 record. Prior to Sunday, Mahomes largely managed games and leaned on the likes of Kenneth Walker III for the burst on offense. Week 10 was a different animal, however. Mahomes exploded for 348 passing yards and five passing touchdowns in a dominant win over the Falcons.

    MAHOMES FIVE TOUCHDOWN PASSES 🔥 pic.twitter.com/G1ZClQomml.

    This was Mahomes' first game with at least five passing touchdowns since Week 1 of the 2022 season.

    Industry observers note that sunday's win put Kansas City back atop the AFC West and in prime position to return to the playoffs in some capacity after a one-year absence in 2025. All that has Mahomes as a shoo-in to win Comeback Player of the Year.

    So, even though we have plenty of time before these awards are handed out, you can start engraving COY and CPOY now.

    How Game Balls work: Six are awarded to standout players from the slate of teams that won their contests, and only one player on a team can get a game ball.

    Gibbs was a man amongst boys in Detroit's Week 10 win over the Patriots in Munich. He finished with 252 yards from scrimmage, which were the second-most in a game in his career. It was also the second-most scrimmage yards in an international game all-time. Moreover, his 28-yard touchdown run (his second of the day) was his 62nd of his career, which is the most by any player in his four seasons in NFL history.

    Penei leads the way for another Jahmyr Gibbs tuddy! pic.twitter.com/EuBi7Y2U4c.

    Industry observers note that jacksonville continues to roll and moved to 7-2 after a 40-23 win over Tennessee. Amid the winning effort, Parker Washington dazzled with some circus catches en route to 152 receiving yards for the day. That set a new career high for the Jags wideout. Dating back to last season, Washington has tallied 992 receiving yards over his last 12 games. That's the most in a 12-game span by a Jaguars player since 2015.

    Parker Washington or Peter Parker?JAXvsTEN on FOX/FOX OneStream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/l02kcfOngG.

    Chase may not have found the end zone, but he was the catalyst for the Bengals offense in a dominant win over the Steelers. The Cincinnati wideout hauled in 11 of his 14 targets for 231 yards. This marks the third time in Chase's career that he's recorded at least 10 catches and 225 receiving yards in a game, which is tied for the most in NFL history.

    Joe Burrow throws it deep to Ja'Marr Chase for the first down 🚀PITvsCIN on NBC/PeacockStream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/o97edw3OV3.

    It has been revealed that kenneth Walker III, who? The Chiefs rookie back filled the shoes of the star back perfectly as he was inactive for Week 10 due to a groin injury. If you didn't look too hard, it was hard to tell the difference between Johnson and Walker in this game. The fifth-round pick out of Nebraska erupted for 171 scrimmage yards and was a key outlet for Mahomes in the passing game, particularly in the red zone. Johnson became just the second player since 1970 with at least 100 rushing yards, 70 receiving yards, and two touchdowns in his first career start.

    Emmett Johnson is too quick 💨CBS | Paramount+ pic.twitter.com/sY1oGo45zY.

    According to recent reports, hubbard was the straw that stirred the drink of the Panthers offense as they outlasted the Saints in Upcoming Orleans. The veteran back accounted for both of Carolina's touchdowns and led the team in rushing as well as receiving. He's just the second player in franchise history to have at least 80 yards rushing and receiving and two rushing touchdowns in a single game, joining Christian McCaffrey (twice). Hubbard helped the Panthers notch their first road win against the Saints since 2023.

    Chuba Hubbard for the lead with 1:49 to play!CARvsNO on FOX/FOX OneStream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/H1nYzGJl8G.

    According to recent reports, mcCaffrey became the first running back in NFL history with two 65-yard touchdown receptions in a game. The 49ers back was doing it all as San Francisco fended off the Cowboys in Dallas to move to 7-1 on the season. Amid a 21-point fourth quarter by the Cowboys, McCaffrey helped keep them at bay with two touchdowns of his own. The final was a 66-yard catch-and-run that proved to be the dagger.

    Don't leave CMC in the open field📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/hGnsBSY5V5.

    Industry observers note that aidan Hutchinson has reportedly suffered a serious knee injury that could knock him out for the foreseeable future. To make matters worse, the injury didn't even come during a play. Instead, Hutchinson was celebrating a third-down sack of Drake Maye during Detroit's opening defensive possession of the afternoon in Germany. After taking down the Patriots quarterback, Hutchinson leaped in the air and then came down awkwardly on his knee.

    In a recent development, the Lions have ruled out star DE Aidan Hutchinson for the game with a knee injury. pic.twitter.com/jR365USNf2.

    Industry observers note that he limped off the field and into the locker room before being ruled out for the rest of the game. Now, it appears that the rest of his season could be in jeopardy.

    One of the dagger moments of Minnesota's victory over the Packers was Myles Price hauling in a third-and-23 pass from Kirk Cousins and taking it 38 yards to the house for a touchdown. Upon hitting paydirt, however, Price was stonewalled by Packers fans as the Vikings receiver tried to troll with a Lambeau Leap. Upon making the jump, the fans stiff-armed Price not once, but twice before he gave up and celebrated with his teammates.

    Best job from the Packers stopping the Vikings all day has been from their fans pic.twitter.com/8ovExbAZBT.

    You could argue that was the best defense from Green Bay all afternoon.

    Sources indicate that as Geno Smith was sidelined due to an injury, rookie quarterback Cade Klubnik was thrust into action. Late in the third quarter, Klubnik threw a brutal interception directly into the arms of a Bills defender. However, the turnover was immediately erased as corner Davison Igbinosun, who recorded the pick, had the ball punched out as he was running up the field. Latest York jumped on the loose ball, so we had two turnovers on a single play.

    Jets throw an INT but get it back on a fumble on the returnBUFvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/f5vRx8b3m1.

    Recent findings suggest that carson Beck's first career interception in the NFL wasn't exactly his fault. The Cardinals rookie made the first start of his career on Sunday and didn't get much help from wideout Devin Duvernay. On a second-and-10 throw from the Rams' 47-yard line, Beck delivered a ball directly into the chest of Duvernay. However, the wideout rolled, the ball bobbled into the air, and was picked off by safety Kamren Kitchens.

    Right spot at the right time for Kam KinchensLARvsAZ on CBS/Paramount+Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/8rDV2qCu39.

    At the time of the pick, it was just a 10-6 lead for Los Angeles. The Rams' offense capitalized on the turnover and scored before halftime, building momentum to run away with the win in the second half.

    It wasn't a banner day for the Jets in their loss to the Bills. Trying to create a spark late, New York called a hook-and-ladder play, but it ended in disaster. Klubnik completed a pass to Garrett Wilson, and as the wideout tried to lateral the football to Kenyon Sadiq, he was hit, which caused the lateral to be botched. The ball hit the turf and was easily picked up by Buffalo.

    Hook-and-ladder didn't go to plan and the Bills wind up with itBUFvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/N8dcLDfRmL.

    McCord made his first career start on Sunday in Indianapolis against the Colts, and the former sixth-round pick had a moment to forget. After a 10-yard penalty backed up the Dolphins to their 10-yard line to begin the second half, McCord faced pressure and was stripped at his own 2-yard line. The ball bounced into the end zone and was scooped up by the Colts for a touchdown.

    PICK-6 FOR DOLPHINS ROOKIE CB CHRIS JOHNSONMIAvsIND on CBS/Paramount+Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/MK3SVpG6M3.

    In a game that saw the Dolphins lose, 24-22, that miscue proved to be the difference.

    Here are some of my quick-hitting takeaways/notes from Week 10:.

    Tech Report: Padres' Mason Miller, Blue Jays' Louis Varland named MLB Relievers of the Year in first-ever BBWAA award

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that san Diego Padres closer Mason Miller and Toronto Blue Jays closer Louis Varland have been named the winners of the first-ever Baseball Writers Association of America Reliever of the Year award.
    • It has been revealed that the BBWAA's Reliever of the Year award is separate from the Mariano Rivera Award and Trevor Hoffman Award, which honor the best relievers in the American League and National League, respectively.
    • Like the other BBWAA awards, the new Reliever of the Year award is voted on by BBWAA members (two per MLB city in each league).
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that san Diego Padres closer Mason Miller and Toronto Blue Jays closer Louis Varland have been named the winners of the first-ever Baseball Writers Association of America Reliever of the Year award. The BBWAA introduced the award this year and, moving forward, will hand it out annually along with Rookies and Managers of the Year, Cy Young, and MVPs.

    It has been revealed that the BBWAA's Reliever of the Year award is separate from the Mariano Rivera Award and Trevor Hoffman Award, which honor the best relievers in the American League and National League, respectively. The Rivera and Hoffman Awards replaced the Delivery Man of the Year Award in 2015 and are voted on by a panel of former relievers, including Rivera and Hoffman.

    Like the other BBWAA awards, the new Reliever of the Year award is voted on by BBWAA members (two per MLB city in each league). Votes were submitted before the beginning of the playoffs, meaning that only regular-season contributions are taken into account.

    The best closer in baseball is the first-ever BBWAA National League Reliever of the Year. Miller was overwhelming from start to finish this past season, pitching to a 1.67 ERA with 129 strikeouts in only 70 innings. He led all pitchers with 3.9 WAR, well ahead of second-place Louie Varland (3.1 WAR), and he led the NL in saves (38) and games finished (57).

    It took 107 years, but the NFL has finally produced its 1,100th final score of all time, and it came on Sunday night in Cincinnati. In an AFC North showdown, the Bengals topped the Steelers 38-18, marking the first time that a game ended with that exact final score.

    It has been revealed that the scorigami only happened because the Steelers scored a garbage-time touchdown in the fourth quarter. With Pittsburgh trailing 38-11, Aaron Rodgers threw a 27-yard TD pass to Pat Freiermuth, and at that point, the Steelers could have gone for two, but instead, they decided to kick the extra point. If the kick had missed, there wouldn't have been a scorigami, because 38-17 has happened before, but Boswell's kick went through and that ultimately gave us the 1,100th final score in NFL history.

    According to recent reports, PIT 18 - CIN 38🚨 SCORIGAMI 🚨That is the 1100th unique score in NFL history, and the 5th of the 2026 season. pic.twitter.com/jIo0wxFPxX.

    For a game to end in a scorigami, you need a few bizarre things to happen and the Steelers definitely provided those.

    It has been revealed that with the Bengals leading 31-3 in the fourth quarter, the Steelers scored a touchdown and decided to go for two, even though it didn't make much sense at that point. They ended up getting the two-point conversion, bringing the score to 38-11. Surprisingly, that final score has actually happened before, so the scorigami didn't become official until Freiermuth got his touchdown later in the fourth quarter. On the second touchdown, the Steelers did NOT go for two, which was a bit bizarre considering they had gone for two on their first score.

    In a recent development, the Bengals did their part of the scorigami by lighting up the scoreboard at Paycor Stadium. Joe Burrow threw for 409 yards and four touchdowns to help the Bengals get to 38 points.

    The Bengals actually had a missed field goal in the game from Evan McPherson and if that would have gone in, we also would have gotten a scorigami, because 41-18 has never happened before in NFL history. The missed kick ended McPherson's franchise-record streak for 25 consecutive field goals.

    Recent findings suggest that when it comes to scorigamis, the Bengals are the hottest team in the NFL right. This is the second straight home game where they've had a scorigami. Before Sunday night, their last home game came in a 43-36 win over the Titans that gave us the 1,098th different final score in NFL history.

    As for the Steelers, this marks the first time they've been involved in a scorigami since a 48-37 playoff loss to the Browns back in January 2021.

    This turned out to be a banner week for scorigamis. Not only did the Bengals and Steelers give us a new final score, but the 49ers' 46-40 win over the Cowboys was also a scorigami.

    Recent findings suggest that this actually marks the second time this season that we've had two scorigamis in one day. It also happened back in Week 1. And I already know what your next question is: This marks the first time since 2017 that we've had two scorigamis in one day happen TWICE in the same season.

    It has been revealed that overall, there have been five scorigamis this year, tied for the most in the 2025 season. Basically, this is turning into the year of the scorigami.

    Sources indicate that milwaukee Brewers ace Jacob Misiorowski has unanimously been named National League Cy Young Award winner for the 2026 Major League Baseball season. He beat out the Phillies' Cristopher Sánchez and the Braves' Chris Sale.

    Sources indicate that misiorowski takes home the honors of the Baseball Writers Association of America vote, which was revealed on Wednesday night. Misiorowski's triumph comes after a stellar age-24 season for the World Series champions:.

    In addition to the top-line numbers above, Misiorowski struck out 37.9% of opposing batters, which is tops in all of MLB and a sky-scraping figure for any pitcher, let alone a starter. Miz also paced the majors in FIP with a mark of 2.17, and his ERA+ of 232 is the 13th-highest figure by a qualifier ever in MLB. Misiorowski's WAR of 6.4 ranked third in the NL behind Sánchez and Jesús Luzardo of the Philadelphia Phillies.

    Industry observers note that misiorowski was perhaps even more notable for his blazing fastball than he was the dominance of his statistical outputs. For the season, Misiorowski averaged 100.6 mph with his heavily used four-seamer, and on multiple occasions during 2026 he threw the fastest pitch on record, including this 105.5 mph offering from June:.

    105.5 MPH FROM JACOB MISIOROWSKI 🔥🔥 pic.twitter.com/wjvkdc7iWE.

    While Misiorowski's playoff performance was not part of the Cy Young criteria – ballots are submitted before the playoffs begin – he did post a 1.89 ERA in four starts this postseason for the Brewers, who wound up winning it all for the first time in franchise history.

    Misiorowski is now the fourth Brewer to win the Cy Young Award. Corbin Burnes won in 2021, and Pete Vuckovich and Rollie Fingers won in 1982 and 1981, respectively, when the franchise was part of the American League.

    In a recent development, given his level of dominance and relative youth, Misiorowski figures to enter the 2027 season as the odds-on favorite to win the hardware again. If he does, he'll become the first back-to-back Cy Young winner in the NL since Jacob deGrom of the Upcoming York Mets in 2018 and 2019.

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil.
    • Hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August.
    • Sources indicate that hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil. The star goalie for the Winnipeg Jets is on the move after being traded to Fresh Jersey on Friday in exchange for four players and two future draft picks. the teams unveiled the move with the Jets receiving Dawson Mercer, Nick Bjugstad, Nico Daws and Alexander Command, plus a 2027 seventh-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.

    Hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August. He mentioned at the time that he had made the request months earlier and tried to keep the situation private.

    Sources indicate that hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No. 130 overall. He's recognized as one of the best goalies in the league as a three-time Vezina Trophy winner. He also helped carry the United States to its first gold medal since 1980 at the 2026 Olympics in February with some incredible saves against Canada in the final game.

    Industry observers note that after trading Jacob Markstom in the offseason, the Devils had a clear need in goal, and this splashy move certainly fills that need. With a talented young core already in place, Newly introduced Jersey's Stanley Cup window is wide open.

    RAISE HELLE!Connor Hellebuyck is a Upcoming Jersey Devil: https://t.co/HCehRGOQI5 pic.twitter.com/dZGNQR16m1.

    For the Jets, it must be a hard pill to swallow when a franchise icon decides to walk out they door, but this trade package should help them as the enter a new era and revamp the roster. Winnipeg got a former first-rounder in Mercer to try and add to a rebuild as well as a veteran presence in Bjugstad. They also acquired a younger goalie in Daws who could fill the role of Hellebuyck at just 25 years old.

    Goaltending has been an glitch in New Jersey for a while now -- even after the team acquired Markstrom from the Calgary Flames in 2024. Markstom never really panned out, and his 13.6 goals allowed above average, per Natural Stat Trick, were a major reason why the Devils missed the postseason last year.

    In the early portion of this season, it was clear that Newly introduced Jersey needed to make a move to upgrade in the crease. Daws and veteran Jake Allen simply aren't a tandem suitable for a Stanley Cup contender, and the numbers backed that up. New Jersey ranks 24th in team save percentage at .877, and the duo of Daws and Allen combined to surrender 2.99 goals above average.

    Once Hellebuyck gets up to game speed, that shouldn't be a problem anymore.

    According to recent reports, in the three-season stretch from 2023-26, Hellebuyck led the NHL with 73.42 goals saved above average, which is 20 goals higher than the next closest netminder. Over that span, Hellebuyck also posted a standard save percentage of .914 and an astronomical high-danger save-percentage of .832.

    Hellebuyck carried less talented teams to the playoffs multiple times in his career. Now on a team loaded with weaponry in their prime -- Jack Hughes, Jesper Bratt and Nico Hischier to name a few -- Hellebuyck could be the final piece to the championship puzzle.

    Sources indicate that in terms of the acquisition cost, it was probably an easy deal for Devils general manager Sunny Mehta to make. The 2029 second-round pick is useless for a team that should be all-in now, Bjugstad is simply a depth piece and Daws now has no path to a starting role with Hellebuyck in town.

    Sources indicate that the most interesting trade chips are Mercer and Command. Mercer flashed major upside with 56 points in his second NHL season, 2022-23, but he hasn't really come close to hitting those heights again. Still, even if he has plateaued, Mercer remains a strong middle-six forward rising into his prime.

    Sources indicate that although Command had his detractors -- and may have been over-drafted at No. 12 overall -- he was a consensus first-round pick last summer. That gives Winnipeg a potential franchise forward it can build around long-term, but Fresh Jersey already has one of the deepest forward groups in the league, especially with the emergence of Arseny Gritsyuk and the acquisition of Luke Evangelista.

    If we're looking for a 3-D chess angle of this deal, it only makes the Devils more appealing for a certain Minnesota Wild defenseman whose brothers just happen to play in Upcoming Jersey already. Grade -- A+.

    Let's get the obvious out of the way first: The Jets were never going to get fair value for Hellebuyck because, at his best, he's the No. 1 goaltender in the world with no equal. That type of excellence can't be replaced.

    Recent findings suggest that that remarked, Winnipeg did fairly well given the circumstances. Hellebuyck made a public trade request, and he wasn't even with the team after sitting out for the entirety of training camp. The entire league knew the Jets had to trade him.

    Hellebuyck's talent created a decent market anyway, but most of the suitors were bona fide Stanley Cup contenders with little in the way of valuable draft capital, and they weren't going to knee cap the roster by sending a key player back in return.

    Sources indicate that with all that taken into consideration, Kevin Cheveldayoff got a solid return. Although Mercer's ceiling may be lower than initially thought, he's a 24-year-old forward who banks roughly 20 goals and 20 assists every season. The kicker with Mercer will be Winnipeg's ability to re-sign him before he hits restricted free agency next summer.

    The addition of Command means Winnipeg now has two forwards selected in the top 12 of the 2026 NHL Draft after taking center Viggo Bjorck themselves. If both of those players deliver on their first-round pedigrees, they could be a terrific one-two punch for the team long-term.

    According to recent reports, daws was a third-round pick in 2020, and despite playing just 13 NHL games since the start of the 2024-25 season, he should give Winnipeg a solid back up option behind Stuart Skinner. It certainly helps that Skinner is off to a great start with his fresh team -- and if Daws develops into a true No. 1 -- it'll be gravy.

    If there's any reason to critique this deal from the Jets' side of things, it's that they didn't get premium draft capital or a surefire up-and-coming prospect. Maybe Command develops into a star, but there's no guarantee he becomes a top-six stud in the NHL.

    The Jets got a lot of good stuff, but they didn't really get anything great, at least not based on what we know in the moment. Because of that, I have to ding Winnipeg a little bit. Grade: B.
