    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    An injury-time penalty from returning hero Raul Jimenez ensured Wolves came away with a point in their Championship opener after Blackburn had produced a comeback.

    Wolves led through Marshall Munetsi’s cool finish on 18 minutes only for Sean McLoughlin’s first Blackburn goal to draw the visitors level on 27 minutes with a well-timed run and header.

    The visitors turned the game around on 48 minutes through Andri Gudjohnsen’s close-range strike only for substitute Jimenez to level the game three minutes into injury time from the spot after Ryan Alebiosu handled the ball in the box. Jimenez and his wife marked his return to Molineux by giving 5,000 fans black scarves emblazoned with the words ‘Si Senor’ - a nod to his song - and Jimenez did not disappoint as he rifled in his penalty.

    LATE DRAMA! 😱Raul Jimenez cooly converts from the penalty spot, deep into added time to save a point for Wolves 🔥 pic.twitter.com/5h2lMxcHNU.

    Recent findings suggest that cesar Peixoto wants Wolves to play with their heads rather than their hearts after the home side rescued a late point in the first game of the Championship season following relegation. Wolves replaced Rob Edwards with Portuguese coach Peixoto during the summer and he felt his side’s loss of organisation allowed Blackburn to take control of the game.

    It has been revealed that peixoto said: “One point is not what we want, we want three points. We lost some organisation in the second half and played more with our hearts and not our heads and brains.

    “We have to keep our mental stability during the 90 minutes because we’re better when we’re organised. We need to play our way with our identity. It’s a lesson for us to understand when we lose organisation it’s more difficult for us and more easy for the opposition.

    According to recent reports, “We’re working hard to bring more solutions [into the club] but we need to work hard with the players we have. It’s the first game, there’s a lot to work on and a lot to improve.”.

    Recent findings suggest that tony Mowbray took charge of Blackburn in the league for the first time since returning to the club for a second stint in the dugout. Rovers recorded their lowest league finish since Mowbray’s first stint in charge of the club last term but the Blackburn boss is confident his side have enough to beat the drop and climb up the table this campaign.

    In a recent development, mowbray said: “Ultimately, it feels like a defeat, it’s a bit disappointing and a bit frustrating. I just felt a lot of decisions were starting to swing their way. It’s harsh to take, I don’t think they deserved a second goal. We asked the players to be brave and we were collectively very strong.

    Recent findings suggest that “Everybody has us relegated, probably on the back of finishing 20th last season and losing a couple of our better players and not spending much money, which is a good motivation for the team. We deserved to win the game, we revealed there’s enough quality to give teams problems and I hope there’s help on the way [in the transfer window].”.

    The first chance of the season came the way of Blackburn as a cross-field pass found Alebiosu down the right, who floated a ball into the box only for an unmarked Oladipo Afolayan to head wide from eight-yards out.

    However, Wolves scored the first goal of the latest campaign when Fer Lopez played a defence-splitting through ball into the path of Munetsi, who coolly found the net with a first time effort from the edge of the penalty area.

    "A vibrant Molineux rejoices!" 🎉Marshall Munetsi cooly slots home for Wolves to give them the lead on the opening night of the Championship season 🥶 pic.twitter.com/tVHdbNv3Hq.

    Blackburn drew level through an unlikely source just nine minutes later as McLoughlin headed in his first-ever goal in English football in more than 150 games when he met Ryoya Morishita’s cross from the right at the near post.

    The home side had chances to retake the lead before the break as Lopez curled a shot narrowly over the top from 20-yards while Kieran Trippier teed up Mateus Mane for a chance as the teenager found the top of the net from distance.

    Blackburn turned the game on its head minutes after the break as Gudjohnsen turned home Afolayan’s deflected ball in from the right from close range to stun Molineux into silence.

    "It's brilliantly worked by Blackburn Rovers!" 💥Andri Guðjohnsen finishes from close range to turn the game around and the visitors the lead 👏 pic.twitter.com/vkKQQezicK.

    Peixoto introduced Jimenez from the bench on the hour mark but even the Mexican could not lift Wolves with Blackburn comfortable for long periods as frustration grew in the stands.

    However, Alebiosu handled Jackson Tchatchoua’s cross from the left in injury time and the referee awarded a spot kick which allowed Jimenez to mark his Wolves return with an equaliser from 12-yards as he sent Balazs Toth the wrong way.

    “I think it is a really harsh one. He [the referee] has to be sure at such a critical time of the game. And I do not think he can be sure. I think he has almost had a guess that he is in the box. It is such a substantial call.”.

    “We see the ref’s position. The fact the ref makes the decision to give the penalty in my opinion, it is a bigger decision to give it then to not. We have got the luxury of the replays and we are still not sure. His whole body is outside the box.”.

Having been in this league a long time, the power of the dressing room is crucial and any motivation tool you can you use is crucial. I think we will be fine. You have to enjoy football and love it. I think the boys enjoyed it tonight.”.

I thought I was outside the box when the ball came in and the decision went against us. They are saying it is in the box and it is frustrating. We dug deep and thought we had it. I cannot fault everyone as we all put in a shift, it was just the final details with the penalty decision. We deserved the three points. If we play like that every week, we will go far in the table.”.

I thought Blackburn were excellent throughout and deservedly took the lead. It is a huge decision [to give the penalty], but in the end Raul Jimenez steps up to get his side the point. [Cesar Peixoto] will be delighted to get something in the end.”.

    When Wolverhampton Wanderers last attacked the Championship under a Portuguese manager new to English football, it proved a vintage season.

    Molineux was under the spell of Nuno Espírito Santo in that 2017-18 campaign, and the major question is whether César Peixoto can lead a repeat nearly a decade later.

    Peixoto was a surprise appointment in June, replacing Rob Edwards, and he has been entrusted with the mission of returning Wolves to the Premier League at the first time of asking.

    “I have changed some things with set-pieces and some things in other moments of the game because I want the team to be organised and understand all the different moments within a match. During pre-season we have scored some goals from high pressing, but we will not be able to press high in every moment of every game. The players have to understand the game and recognise what each moment requires. It is important that we work as a team. When we can press high, we’ll press high. When we need to defend in a mid-block, we will stay organised. When the opposition pushes us deeper, which will sometimes happen, we have to be organised there as well.

    Sources indicate that “There are a lot of crosses in the Championship, for example, so the team needs to understand what to do in those situations. We want to play our football, be offensive and react strongly when we lose the ball, but we also need to understand the different moments of the game. I think we are at a good level to attack the Championship.”.

    It has been revealed that the 2026/27 Championship season kicks off at Molineux as Wolves host Blackburn, with the home side hoping to put the bad memories of last season firmly behind them. There are latest playoff rules in place for this season, with six places now up for grabs in the play-offs.

    In a recent development, wolves are aiming to return to the Premier League at the first attempt, having endured a miserable season in the top flight last year as they finished bottom with just three wins to their name. It has been a summer of change at the club as they chose to change managers. Rob Edwards lost his job in what was a shock move and was replaced by 46-year-old Cesar Peixoto, with this being his first head coaching position outside of his home country Portugal. Back in 2017/18, Wolves won the Championship title led by Peixoto’s compatriot Nuno Espirito Santo.

    Recent findings suggest that “I am ready,” Peixoto told Wolves’ club website. “We have worked very hard during pre-season, and I think we have had a great pre-season. All the players have worked very, very hard and they understand what I want from them. I am ready and confident going into the first game. Football is football, whether it is in Portugal or England, but there are different characteristics to the game here. We have watched, observed and analysed the Championship. We did that work before I came to the club, so we know what to expect.

    According to recent reports, “It is going to be a tough season with good teams, but we are prepared to fight for the three points game after game and week after week. We know what we want from the team and we know what our significant goal is. We’re going to work very hard and fight to achieve that goal.”.

    They have brought in vast experience on the player side in the shape of Kieran Trippier and Raul Jimenez, who is back at Molineux three years after leaving for Fulham. Although they have lost Brazilian midfielder Joao Gomes to Aston Villa, most of their squad has stayed intact as they pursue promotion back to the top flight. It is a special year for the club as they celebrate their 150th anniversary.

    Sources indicate that blackburn, led by experienced manager Tony Mowbray, did not enjoy a great season in the Championship last year, finishing down in 20th place and just five points above the relegation zone. 14 years have now passed since Blackburn last played in the top flight.

    According to recent reports, “I think it is a tough start,” Mowbray said. “On paper, I would suggest the first couple of games, particularly, jumped out as a tough start. One of the Premier League sides from last season, away from home. They have got a very talented squad, a pretty expensive squad. They have got some very good individual talent. Yet, there is an argument to say they have not won many football matches in the last calendar year. So, what we get, we will have to wait and see.”.

    Industry observers note that these sides last met in the FA Cup during the 2024/25 season, with Wolves winning that fourth-round tie 2-0 thanks to goals from Matheus Cunha and Gomes, both of whom are now plying their trade elsewhere. The omens would appear to be on Wolves’ side as they are unbeaten in their last eight league meetings with Blackburn. Both sides progressed to the second round of the League Cup last weekend, with Wolves beating Port Vale 3-0 and Blackburn overcoming Burton Albion 2-1.

    Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer again declines to support DC Christian Parker after struggles, brutal loss to 49ers

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Brian Schottenheimer, at least publicly, isn't backing his defensive coordinator.
    • The Cowboys head coach didn't directly support defensive coordinator Christian Parker on Monday, one day after a brutal showing from the Dallas defense in its 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers.
    • "We're still working through the process, talking to the guys is the first step," Schottenheimer remarked, via The Dallas Morning News.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Brian Schottenheimer, at least publicly, isn't backing his defensive coordinator.

    The Cowboys head coach didn't directly support defensive coordinator Christian Parker on Monday, one day after a brutal showing from the Dallas defense in its 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers.

    Instead, he said everything is still under review.

    "We're still working through the process, talking to the guys is the first step," Schottenheimer remarked, via The Dallas Morning News. "At the end of the day, there's a lot of things that we need to clean up as a football team. That starts with me.".

    The 49ers racked up 584 yards of offense and averaged 9.4 yards per play in the win on Sunday. They ran for 214 yards, too, and put up 29 points and 340 yards in the second half alone. It was simply an offensive clinic that the Cowboys couldn't stop time and time again.

    The 584 yards that Dallas allowed was the most they've allowed in a home game in franchise history.

    Schottenheimer stated after the game that he thought the defense was "unacceptable," and he called the tackling "atrocious.".

    "At the end of the day, we tackled like s**t in the second half," he said.

    Sources indicate that dallas' defensive challenges are nothing new. They've been a problem all season, and it's led to louder and louder calls to make a change at defensive coordinator. Parker is in his first season in the role, which also marks his first coordinator job in the NFL.

    Though he declined to support Parker again on Monday, Schottenheimer did not say he was going to make a change.

    According to recent reports, "I'm not saying that," he said. "I'm saying we're still in the process of going through all the film and evaluation of where we stand today.".

    Perhaps more importantly, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones did back Parker on Sunday afternoon.

    "Again, it's what it is," Jones said postgame. "He's a young coach in his first year of coordinating and calling the plays. So you have to say that you would hope you could win games like the last that we've lost.

    Industry observers note that "I'll weigh his early times. I've been with teams that had some pretty good coordinators on defense that ended up winning Super Bowls.".

    But instead of following Jones' lead, Schottenheimer said simply that they are "taking a deep dive" and "looking at everything.".

    During his weekly appearance on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, all Jones would say is that Parker's position has come up.

    "We're talking about that, but I'm not going to talk about it here," Jones noted. "But we are talking about those things.".

    The Cowboys are still in the playoff hunt despite their 4-6 record, thanks to a rough NFC East. They are only two games behind the New York Giants. They'll take on the Tennessee Titans next weekend. But the Cowboys haven't won a Super Bowl since the 1995 season, and this team doesn't appear capable of ending that streak.

    The frustration that fans feel, vice president Stephen Jones mentioned, is being felt internally, too.

    Recent findings suggest that "I certainly understand their frustration because there's no doubt that we're frustrated," the younger Jones remarked on 105.3 The Fan. "We feel like the way we're playing ball right now is unacceptable. Our fans certainly deserve better.".

    Whether the outcry and issues on defense result in a change at defensive coordinator before the end of the season, however, is still anybody's guess.

    #15546. Steelers' receiver problem proves they made a massive NFL trade deadline mistake

    📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (772 w)

    Steelers' receiver problem proves they made a massive NFL trade deadline mistake

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (772 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Pittsburgh Steelers lost Sunday night's game to the Cincinnati Bengals days before the game even started.
    • Hours after Josh Downs -- whom the Steelers were reportedly interested in acquiring before the deadline -- scored a touchdown in his Kansas City Chiefs debut, Pittsburgh fans were forced to sit through another game of watching DK Metcalf play dodgeball and Aaron Rodgers desperately looking for Jaylen Warren in the flat with no open options downfield.
    • Industry observers note that rodgers did not complete a pass until late in the first half.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Pittsburgh Steelers lost Sunday night's game to the Cincinnati Bengals days before the game even started. OK, that might be a stretch. But the Steelers' decision not to acquire a receiver before the trade deadline has aged faster than milk on a hot summer day.

    Hours after Josh Downs -- whom the Steelers were reportedly interested in acquiring before the deadline -- scored a touchdown in his Kansas City Chiefs debut, Pittsburgh fans were forced to sit through another game of watching DK Metcalf play dodgeball and Aaron Rodgers desperately looking for Jaylen Warren in the flat with no open options downfield.

    Industry observers note that rodgers did not complete a pass until late in the first half. At that point, it was already 17-0 Bengals, a lead that swelled to 24-3 before intermission. It was 31-3 in the third before the Steelers finally found the end zone early in the fourth quarter. Ironically, the score was courtesy of Metcalf, but it was way too little, too late. Pittsburgh later tacked on another late score in garbage time in what was a 38-18 loss.

    There was plenty of evidence before the deadline that the Steelers needed help at receiver. Metcalf entered Sunday with just one touchdown and only 33 catches on 64 targets. Germie Bernard has played well for a rookie, but he's not a No. 2 receiver, at least not now.

    Industry observers note that despite their lack of weaponry, the Steelers were 6-2 heading into their bye week, which coincided with the trade deadline. Pittsburgh reportedly discussed trades involving Downs, Brian Thomas Jr., and Calvin Ridley. Thomas and Ridley were not traded, but Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick were sent to Kansas City in exchange for 2027 fourth- and fifth-round picks. A very reasonable trade that the Steelers should have tried to make.

    There are two likely reasons why the Steelers didn't trade for a receiver. Pittsburgh probably didn't want to give up too many future draft picks that could be used to acquire its next franchise quarterback, and it still has confidence in its receiving corps.

    Let's address the second reason first. Pittsburgh had an eight-game sample size to assess their situation at receiver. It was clear before the deadline that reinforcements were needed, even with the prospect of Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman's possible returns from injuries (Pittman, an expensive offseason acquisition, has seven catches this season and hasn't played since Week 4).

    Sources indicate that regarding future draft picks, that's the price the Steelers continue to pay for not having found their long-term solution at quarterback. The Steelers have three other quarterbacks on their roster (including rookie Drew Allar), so there's a good chance that Pittsburgh won't spend a high pick on a quarterback in 2027, anyway. Pittsburgh's current 2026 projection suggests they won't have a high draft pick again. That has been an ongoing glitch for a team that still hasn't found Ben Roethlisberger's long-term successor.

    Regardless of the reason, the Steelers' lack of movement at the deadline raises the following question: what was the point of bringing back Rodgers? If the Steelers were serious about maximizing their strong start (like the Chiefs and Jaguars did) in Rodgers' final season, they would have gotten a receiver at the deadline, among other things. Instead, the Steelers stood pat and were blown out on Sunday night by a Bengals team that moved past them for first place in the AFC North.

    Pittsburgh's situation at receiver is a mess, but that's not its only problem. The defense was a disaster on Sunday night. They had no answer for Joe Burrow, who sliced and diced Pittsburgh's zone coverage.

    Recent findings suggest that cincinnati, winners of five straight games, appears to be not only the front-runner to win the North, but possibly the entire AFC. Conversely, the Steelers are a decent team that has benefitted from an easy schedule.

    It has been revealed that pittsburgh faces only two teams with winning records from here on out, so it's very possible that the Steelers can get to 10 wins for a fourth straight season. That's far from a guarantee, however. The Steelers suffered a serious loss Sunday night when guard Mason McCormick was carted off the field in the second quarter. While the severity of his injury wasn't immediately known, it appears that Pittsburgh will have to move forward without him.

    Recent findings suggest that even if the Steelers reach 10 wins and earn a fourth straight playoff berth, their season appears headed for a disappointing finish. Rodgers deserved better than that in his final season.

    Celtics vs. 76ers winners and losers: Jayson Tatum outduels Jaylen Brown, but Paul George steals the show

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that nick Nurse nailed it.
    • "This is probably one -- maybe the one -- that people were circling in the summertime when the schedule came out," Nurse noted.
    • Sources indicate that nick Nurse on his morning conversation with Jaylen Brown and hype surrounding the grudge match with the Celtics.“This is probably one — maybe the one — that people were circling in the summer time when the schedule came out.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that nick Nurse nailed it. A lot of people had a lot to say in advance of the Celtics and 76ers facing each other for the first time this season, but Philadelphia's coach summed it up pretty well before the two teams tipped off on Tuesday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

    "This is probably one -- maybe the one -- that people were circling in the summertime when the schedule came out," Nurse noted.

    Sources indicate that nick Nurse on his morning conversation with Jaylen Brown and hype surrounding the grudge match with the Celtics.“This is probably one — maybe the one — that people were circling in the summer time when the schedule came out. It’s finally here.” pic.twitter.com/CdBoE576iI.

    In a recent development, he wasn't kidding. From the moment Jaylen Brown was traded to the Sixers, the hype and drama surrounding the first meeting between him and his old team -- and his longtime running mate-turned-rival, Jayson Tatum -- have been seemingly endless. While Tatum tried to lower the heat on the simmering feud, claiming that he was "caught off guard as much as the rest of the world" when Brown was shipped to Philly, Brown was all too happy to add rhetorical fuel to the fire, saying there might not be beef between the two players, but there was some "lamb chops and gravy" and warning his former teammate to "stay ready at all times.".

    By Tuesday, there wasn't much left unsaid. When Brown was asked whether he would talk to Tatum prior to the game, he dismissed the idea: "There's nothing to talk about. He's on his side, I'm on my side. We're playing basketball. Both of us are trying to win. So there's nothing to talk about. Check the ball up.".

    The old saying about being careful what you wish for comes to mind. They checked the ball up and the Celtics ran the Sixers off their floor in what ended up as a blowout 123-101 win for Boston. Aside from the actual victory for the Celtics that moved them ahead of the Sixers in the standings and into first place in the Eastern Conference, here are the winners and losers from the most anticipated game of the season to date, including the under-discussed player in the Brown-to-Philly deal having the performance of the night.

    The Sixers beating the Celtics in the first round of the playoffs last year was the outlier, not the rule. Boston tends to get the better of Philly in substantial games. Tatum and the Celtics reminded everyone about that on Tuesday. He finished with 21 points, six rebounds, four assists and two blocks. And a whole lot of bragging rights.

    We got some Tatum vs. Brown one-on-one matchups early, with Tatum getting the better of the duel at the defensive end.

    Jayson Tatum forces the turnover on Jaylen Brown in their first iso of the game.📺 NBA on NBC and Peacock pic.twitter.com/IOStW8Kk93.

    And while his most memorable play didn't come against Brown, Tatum still had the highlight of the evening when he threw down a monster dunk on LeBron James.

    JAYSON TATUM WITH THE POSTER ON LEBRON JAMES!📺 NBA on NBC and Peacock pic.twitter.com/LOXzzT0FjJ.

    Brown was right. There wasn't anything left to talk about. Tatum did his talking on the court.

    This was always going to be a zero-sum game. Tatum won, Brown lost. But the way Brown went down wasn't great as far as optics and narratives go. He was held to a season-low 13 points, got in foul trouble, had four turnovers and was a game-worst minus-27. Oof.

    It has been revealed that apart from a nice dunk in the first half, it was a game for Brown to forget. Making matters worse, the guy he got traded for had a night to remember.

    "I'm a bit frustrated, honestly," Brown noted after the game. "I wanted to perform better for my team. Foul trouble kind of derailed me a little bit, but it happens. It's unfortunate, but now we got to just move on to the next.".

    In a recent development, when the Sixers traded George, it seemed like a magic trick by fresh president of basketball operations Mike Gansey. George played just 78 largely unspectacular games over two seasons in Philly. Beyond that, he's six years older than Brown and still had two years and more than $110 million left on his deal.

    It has been revealed that so naturally, George has looked like the best version of himself since leaving Philly and going to Boston. His hot start to the season continued on Tuesday with him dropping 36 points on 14 for 22 shooting from the field, including making six of his 11 3-point attempts. He was so good against his former team that at one point he inspired NBC's Noah Eagle on the play-by-play call to exclaim, "PG-13 has turned Rated R." (Prepackaged, but still a great line.).

    According to recent reports, PAUL GEORGE HAS 30 POINTSVINTAGE PG. 🔥🔥🔥 pic.twitter.com/AH8RI4yVnp.

    Sources indicate that it was supposed to be either Tatum or Brown's night, but George ended up commanding the biggest spotlight with how well he played. He also got the last laugh after an interaction with a Philly fan who, according to George, "dropped the ball on the ground like I'm a dog to go fetch or go get it instead of passing the ball to me like a normal fan." In response, George said he "rolled him a middle finger.".

    Looks like Paul George may have also flipped out a fan (or someone) after that three pic.twitter.com/LecXldKldE.

    Industry observers note that with Brad Stevens in the front office and Joe Mazzulla on the sideline, the Celtics have long had a theory of the case: Take more 3s than their opponents and bet that they'll make more. That gamble has served them well more often than not. They won a championship that way while leading the league in 3-point attempts and makes per game during the 2023-24 season. The strategy did not work as well against the Sixers in the last postseason, but the Celtics have made peace with the approach, win or lose.

    Nothing has changed. Boston still loves to fire away from deep, and that's exactly what the Celtics did against the Sixers on Tuesday. Boston shot 45% from beyond the arc (22 for 49), compared to just 30% for Philadelphia (11 for 37).

    In a recent development, when the outside shots are falling for the Celtics, they're tough to beat. No one knows that better than Jaylen Brown.

    Why shake hands or hug when you can just turn your back and offer a cold shoulder instead?

    The pregame moment between Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown.📺 NBA on NBC and Peacock pic.twitter.com/P4iclUnqZ5.

    When asked about this moment, Brown told reporters he "wasn't paying attention" when Tatum attempted to greet him.

    "I'm just focused on coming out and doing what's best for my team. Everything else was just, to be honest, I wasn't paying attention," Brown stated. "Credit to Jayson, he played well tonight. Credit to the Celtics, they executed, they shot the hell out of the ball and were the better team tonight.".

    Arguably the best part of Brown ignoring Tatum was Tatum then immediately going to LeBron James for an intricate handshake and embrace right afterward.

    Looks like Jayson Tatum tried to dap up/hug Jaylen Brown but it wasn’t reciprocated pic.twitter.com/6iMOrpvmmD.

    Pretty much everyone was asked about Tatum and Brown, from Joe Mazzulla talking about how the trade could have been handled differently, to Payton Pritchard weighing in on whether there was beef between them, to Paul George taking credit for helping the Sixers "land a future piece" in Brown by getting traded (all the lols there).

    The winner, though, was 76ers guard Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, who, unlike Pritchard, didn't try to minimize the suspected animosity between Tatum and Brown -- or at least what appears to be some obvious hurt feelings from Brown's side. When Caldwell-Pope was asked about the situation, he pointed to a social media interaction as proof of what we all suspected anyway.

    "I don't know what the tension was before JB left," Caldwell-Pope stated. "All I know is when he wrote on the comments when JT did that little interview, that's all I know. That's all I need to know.".

    Kentavious Caldwell-Pope says Jaylen Brown mindset going into the matchup with the Celtics is he’s trying to BTA:“I don’t know what the tension was before but before JB left all I know is when he wrote on the comments when JT did that little interview, that’s all I know, that’s… pic.twitter.com/Co8Wkh0APS.

    Recent findings suggest that if you somehow missed it, "that little interview" was Tatum claiming that he found out about the trade when everyone else did -- which prompted Brown to pop up in the comments with a cap emoji, essentially calling Tatum a liar. Credit to Caldwell-Pope for calling it like it is rather than pretending.

    Speaking of pretending, Nurse was asked about how Brown was approaching the game and reached into his bag of coach clichés for a classic favored by so many in his profession during times like these.

    According to recent reports, "He's approaching it as another game," Nurse noted. "Major game. He's excited for the opportunity, but he wasn't expressing it in a personal way. He said this is a really good test for our team, and I agree with him.".

    Nick Nurse on how Jaylen Brown is approaching tonight’s game:“He's approaching it as another game. Big game. He's excited for the opportunity, but he wasn't expressing it in a personal way. He mentioned this is a really good test for our team, and I agree with him.” pic.twitter.com/6MiBQXBVCx.

    It has been revealed that brown advised Tatum to stay ready at all times and everyone from the fans to the media dined out on the pork chops and gravy remarks for weeks in advance. It's hard to sell that as just another game.

    Full marks to whoever came up with the song selection for Celtics shootaround on Tuesday.

    In a recent development, celtics shootaround underway with “why can’t we be friends” playing. pic.twitter.com/EJV3A8pQKL.

    According to recent reports, not long before tip-off, ESPN's Shams Charania reported that Tatum and Brown had a "heart-to-heart" in France prior to the trade. According to the report, the meeting occurred shortly after Brown was dangled in a failed trade attempt for Giannis Antetokounmpo, but before he was sent to Philadelphia.

    That sounded pretty juicy, except to hear longtime NBA guard Evan Turner tell it on social media, "this didn't happen." Not to be outdone, Carmelo Anthony also weighed in on the topic, saying that being around the two in France was "weird.".

    Carmelo Anthony says the energy was weird with Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown in France when they we're all together just days before the trade happened pic.twitter.com/NQ0rGnt5Vh.

    In a recent development, turner's source on the subject was unclear, but he was pretty emphatic about the denial, insisting in the comments to the story that the pair never spoke. Not sure that anyone predicted Turner coming off the top rope to smack down an NBA report, but if this ends with him or Carmelo becoming the newly introduced Woj, we're all in for a treat.

    The trade deadline is all about the deals that actually get done, but what about the ones that never cross the finish line? The Bengals learned a hard lesson about the compensatory pick formula on Tuesday and called off a trade because of it. They were in agreement with the Eagles on a swap that would send Arnold Ebiketie to Cincinnati in return for a 2027 sixth-round pick but backed out when they realized the ramifications. Our Jordan Dajani explained the bizarre situation when he labeled the Bengals as the deadline's biggest losers.

    That's an example of what not to do if you're inside an NFL front office. But as we shift our focus back to the trades that did come to fruition, we have to recognize the masterclass the 49ers put on. They landed Keenan Allen on Tuesday to add to a haul that already included DeForest Buckner. In securing much-needed wide receiver help, they became one of four teams to receive an "A" grade on our trade deadline report card. For context, here's a look at the rest of the NFC West:.

    According to recent reports, defensive players are important, too! In fact, many of the splashiest moves included defensive linemen and defensive backs. Take Amani Hooker, for instance. The Bills gave up a second-round pick to land the NFL's interception leader in one of the top five deals of the deadline.

    It's hard to say that any team got better than the Jaguars (they made three splashes and boosted an already prolific defense), but the Chiefs also upgraded significantly. Josh Downs is the newest member of their wide receiver group by way of a win-win trade with the Colts.

    Recent findings suggest that pete Prisco finalized his latest set of NFL Power Rankings before the last-minute hustle of trade deadline moves, so the dip the Vikings took ahead of Week 10 emphasizes just how notable it was for them to add Kirk Cousins. Minnesota was the biggest faller of the week, down five spots to No. 11. Most teams' trades (or lack thereof) were already factored into the equation, though, so it should not come as a surprise to see the deadline's most active franchises check in at the top of the pecking order. Each of the top six teams made at least one trade.

    A little further down, the Packers jumped into the top 10 without adding to their roster. A certain superstar edge rusher should return to action by the end of the month, though.

    We're in the throes of spooky season, and fittingly, the Newly introduced Jersey Devils just got a lot scarier with the acquisition of superstar goaltender Connor Hellebuyck.

    In a recent development, one of the best goaltenders in the world, Hellebuyck fills the biggest need on the Devils roster. With him in between the pipes and an electrifying group of forwards, New Jersey will be a force in the Eastern Conference.

    Don't take my word for it. Just look at what the Devils did Tuesday against the Dallas Stars. In his first start with the team, Hellebuyck stopped 17 of the 18 shots he faced -- allowing one goal on 2.04 expected goals against -- in a 5-1 victory.

    In a recent development, nico Hischier, Jack Hughes and Luke Hughes each had multi-point nights as the Devils took full advantage of the chances they created against a stout Dallas team. This type of game has to be exactly what general manager Sunny Mehta envisioned when he swung the deal for Hellebuyck.

    Moving forward, the Devils will be burdened with the pressure that comes along with being a bona fide Cup contender. For a franchise that's fallen short of expectations a few times lately, that can be a scary prospect, and it inspired a special Halloween edition of the NHL Power Rankings in which I highlight the scariest thing about each team.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Another NFL Sunday is in the books, with just one game left in Week 10 as the Baltimore Ravens host the LA Chargers on "Monday Night Football.".

    Sunday kicked off with a bang as the Detroit Lions and Fresh England Patriots faced off in Munich, Germany, with injuries to two stars that will have all eyes drawn as the new week plays out. Lions star defensive end Aidan Hutchinson suffered what is feared to be a season-ending ACL tear while celebrating a sack against Patriots quarterback Drake Maye … who suffered an ankle injury on that very sack, which knocked him out of the game and could cost him the season.

    Week 10 also offered us our first look at Las Vegas Raiders No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza as a starter. He led scoring drives on each of the Raiders' first two possessions and entered halftime with a 10-7 lead over the Seattle Seahawks, but Drew Lock rallied with two passing touchdowns in the third quarter to take the lead, improving to 3-0 as a starter for Seattle this season. Raiders star tight end Brock Bowers exited the loss with an ankle injury.

    Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest NFL news, injury updates and more coming out of Week 10.

    Jones would not elaborate with the hosts about the discussions regarding the Cowboys' defense and Parker's standing within the organization.

    Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheim didn't directly support Parker on Monday, one day after a brutal showing from the Dallas defense in its 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers.

    Instead, he said everything is still under review.

    "We're still working through the process, talking to the guys is the first step," Schottenheimer said, via The Dallas Morning News. "At the end of the day, there's a lot of things that we need to clean up as a football team. That starts with me.".

    The 26-year-old Joseph has not played this season due to a knee injury that limited him to only six games last season.

    Barring a setback, Joseph, a 2024 First-team All-Pro, will be on the field when the Lions take on the Buccaneers in Week 11.

    Dallas Cowboys right guard Tyler Booker sustained a high ankle sprain during the second quarter of Sunday's 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers and is expected to miss at least four weeks, according to several reports.

    Such an injury usually requires a recovery timeline of four to six weeks, but the Cowboys are hopeful that Booker can return in three to four weeks.

    Starting cornerback DaRon Bland also suffered a right high ankle sprain during the Cowboys' first defensive series while trying to tackle 49ers receiver Deebo Samuel Sr. He had dealt with an injury to his left ankle during the previous week of practice.

    The team is also considering whether or not to put both plalyers on injured reserve with a possible four-week absence. However, Dallas has a bye for Week 14, which could allow them to stay on the active roster.

    The Chicago Bears should have running back Kyle Monangai available for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints.

    Monangai has been out for more than a month with both a thumb injury and turf toe.

    Sources indicate that "It's something I can manage now," he mentioned, via ESPN's Courtney Cronin. "The time off was needed though for sure. I feel in a much better spot than I was a month ago.".

    The two big Super Bowl odds movers this week resulted from one play on Sunday, when Aidan Hutchinson sacked Drake Maye and then Hutchinson proceeded to injure himself on the celebration.

    Unfortunately, for the Lions, it's reportedly a torn ACL for Hutchinson, which would sideline him for the rest of the season. Detroit, despite a 7-2 record, moved from 18-1 to 20-1 odds to win the Super Bowl (11th-best odds). It's also reportedly a "significant lower-leg injury" for Maye, and with a 5-5 record already in a crowded AFC field, Upcoming England's Super Bowl odds tumbled from 28-1 entering the week to 66-1.

    According to recent reports, the Chargers are bringing in some reinforcements ahead of a Monday night clash against the Ravens. The team announced Monday that they have activated tight end David Njoku and linebacker Denzel Perryman from injured reserve.

    Njoku has been marked out with a fibula injury, while Perryman has been out with a pectoral injury. Both players were listed as "questionable" heading into this weekend, but were full participants in practice on Saturday.

    In related moves, Los Angeles placed guard/tackle Branson Taylor on IR and elevated defensive lineman Myles Adams from the practice squad.

    The 0-8 Chargers are trying to pick up their first win of the year against Baltimore.

    Industry observers note that the Raiders have some good news on star tight end Brock Bowers, who exited Sunday's loss to the Seahawks with an ankle injury. Though the injury, which occurred during the first quarter, initially appeared concerning, Las Vegas head coach Klint Kubiak noted Monday that things were better than originally feared.

    In a press conference, Kubiak noted that the team was "still evaluating" Bowers, but that the tight end will be day-to-day with the injury.

    "It's not as bad as we thought, but still is a significant injury, so we'll keep monitoring him," Kubiak noted.

    Bowers, who missed the first two games of the season after undergoing minor knee surgery, leads Las Vegas in receiving with 676 yards and six touchdowns in eight games.

    Industry observers note that upcoming York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn was hired by the team thanks to his excellence as a defensive coordinator. But after the team struggled on defense during Glenn's first year as head coach, he decided to take over defensive play-calling duties in 2026.

    Industry observers note that that change lasted just nine games. Glenn told reporters Monday he gave up defensive play-calling ahead of the team's 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills in Week 10, per ESPN.

    Industry observers note that glenn stated the move was made to help the team win games. He added that while Jets defensive coordinator Brian Duker called plays Sunday, Glenn was "very involved" in the team's scheme.

    "I've said this and I will continue to do this: Anything I can do as a head coach to help us win games, I'm willing to do it," Glenn said. "I'm not afraid to do that. So I gave him the lead, but I was very involved in what we ran.".

    Industry observers note that the change appeared positive initially, as the Jets (2-8) gave up just 10 points in the first half Sunday. But Buffalo's offense got rolling in the second half, allowing the team to pull away.

    Recent findings suggest that the Jets ultimately gave up 31 points in a loss to the Bills. Though, in Duker's defense, facing Josh Allen in your first game as a defensive play-caller is among the toughest asks in the NFL. The Bills rank first in the NFL with 31.9 points scored per game. In that sense, Duker's defense actually held the team under its season-long average … barely. The Jets still allowed 31 points, so the team shouldn't start popping the champagne just yet.

    If everything goes according to plan, star Green Bay defensive end Micah Parsons should be returning from injury sooner rather than later.

    In a press conference on Monday, Packers head coach Matt LaFleur told reporters that the "blueprint" is for Parsons to play in Green Bay's next game, with the team taking on the Los Angeles Rams the day before Thanksgiving.

    "Well, that's my plan, but I think my plan's been different than everybody else's the whole time," LaFleur noted with a smile, after being asked if the plan was for Parsons to return to the field in L.A. "There's still a couple more hurdles for him to clear before we can definitively say that he's a go. He's showing progress, but we'll see where he is by the end of the week.".

    Parsons was cleared for practice earlier this month, 11 months after tearing his ACL.

    Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jordan Addison has a thumb injury that requires surgery and will miss multiple weeks.

    Head coach Kevin O'Connell revealed the injury on Monday, telling reporters that Addison sustained a "freak" injury in practice last week. O'Connell did not reveal the precise nature of Addison's injury or how he sustained it.

    Addison missed Sunday's win over the Green Bay Packers and may need a stint on injured reserve, which would require him to miss a minimum of four games.

    Seattle Seahawks running back George Holani suffered a sprained MCL in Week 10's 21-13 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reports.

    Seattle has a bye next week, so the hope is that will provide enough recovery time to avoid putting Holani on injured reserve, according to Rapoport.

    Recent findings suggest that holani did not have a carry in Sunday's contest after leaving in the first quarter. In 10 games this season, he has 117 yards on 37 carries with 1 touchdown. Additionally, Holani has registered 12 receptions for 88 yards.

    With starting QB Baker Mayfield dealing with a lower-body injury through the team's bye week, Tampa Bay opted to sign veteran Cooper Rush to the roster, his agents declared.

    Rush began the season with the Falcons. In two games, he threw for 229 yards with a touchdown and four interceptions. He was released once Michael Penix Jr. and Tua Tagovailoa were healthy enough to return.

    Tampa Bay has the Detroit Lions, Carolina Panthers, Los Angeles Chargers and Baltimore Ravens over the next month.

    Recent findings suggest that the Dolphins have waived veteran kicker Zane Gonzalez. He played four games for Miami this year.

    Gonzalez ends his Dolphins tenure 6 of 10 on field goals and 6 of 7 on extra-point attempts.

    The Miami kicker missed two field goals (47 yards, 51 yards) and an extra point in the Dolphins' 24 to 22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.

    Miami at the moment has no other kicker in the organization.

    Detroit Lions pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson reportedly tore his ACL while celebrating a sack of Drake Maye, per NFL Network.

    Recent findings suggest that early reports Sunday suggested Hutchinson was dealing with a "significant" knee injury. Initial tests reportedly confirmed as much Monday.

    Hutchinson will miss the rest of the 2026 NFL season as he recovers from the injury. It's unclear whether his availability will be impacted next season.

    The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are at the moment on bye, but unfortunately, they are still in the news.

    Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield is dealing with a lower-leg injury that he suffered during last week's loss to the Chicago Bears, NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported on Sunday morning.

    According to recent reports, mayfield's status is uncertain for Tampa Bay's Week 11 matchup with the Detroit Lions. It is unclear where Mayfield picked up the injury against the Bears. The quarterback was sacked four times, but he never left the game. This week, he was reportedly spotted in a walking boot, rehabbing and resting.

    According to recent reports, this would not be the first time this season the Buccaneers have played without their starting quarterback. Mayfield dislocated his thumb in Week 3, which kept him out for three games. Tampa Bay turned to undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels, who went 1-2 as the starter.

    According to recent reports, mayfield has played in six games so far this season and is 2-4. He has not looked like himself all year, throwing for just 922 yards, 3 touchdowns and 4 interceptions. In a bad-weather Week 8 game against the Atlanta Falcons, he finished 0-for-3 for zero yards in the team's 16-0 win, making infamous history.

    It has been revealed that A frustrating season for Los Angeles Chargers wideout Ladd McConkey will continue in Week 10. While the receiver was initially listed as questionable on the team's final injury report, he will not play against the Baltimore Ravens on "Monday Night Football.".

    In a recent development, mcConkey was ruled out for the game due to back spasms. He did not travel with the team to Baltimore, the Chargers announced.

    McConkey has been limited by multiple injuries throughout the regular season. He was held to just 35 yards in Week 2 thanks to a rib injury and missed Week 5 due to a foot issue.

    Recent findings suggest that he caught just one ball in Week 6 before resting during the bye week. While the wideout looked to be close to 100 percent with an 86-yard performance in Week 8, McConkey missed Week 9 with back spasms. The injury reportedly occurred just before game time. He was expected to play in the contest.

    Those back spasms have apparently continued to plague McConkey throughout the week. He was held out of practice each day leading up to Week 10, though the team still held some hope he would play, initially giving him the questionable tag.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Most of the attention going into Tuesday's clash between the Eastern Conference's top two seeds went to Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown.
    • Yet it was ultimately the other player involved in that blockbuster, Paul George, who wound up stealing the show.
    • According to recent reports, despite that stellar outing, it was what happened during a stoppage in the fourth quarter that became one of the night's most notable moments.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Most of the attention going into Tuesday's clash between the Eastern Conference's top two seeds went to Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown. The two former Boston Celtics teammates squared off for the first time since the latter was traded to the Philadelphia 76ers, and based on both the back and forth between them in the press and the chilly reception Brown gave Tatum on the floor, there's a fair bit of animosity between the two.

    Yet it was ultimately the other player involved in that blockbuster, Paul George, who wound up stealing the show. After two years in Philadelphia, George returned to his old stomping grounds for the first time as a Celtic and led all scorers with 36 points in Boston's 123-101 victory.

    According to recent reports, despite that stellar outing, it was what happened during a stoppage in the fourth quarter that became one of the night's most notable moments. After drilling his fourth 3-pointer to give the Celtics a 100-82 lead, the 76ers called timeout. As George retreated to Boston's bench, he gave the Philadelphia crowd the middle finger.

    Looks like Paul George may have also flipped out a fan (or someone) after that three pic.twitter.com/LecXldKldE.

    In the moment, it felt as if George might be taking some revenge against the team that shipped him out over the summer. As George explained after the game, however, it wasn't anger at the entire 76ers fanbase or the team itself that motivated the middle finger. It was one fan in particular.

    "There was a fan being an asshole," George explained. "Ball rolled to him. He looked me dead in my eyes, dropped the ball on the ground as if like I'm a dog to go fetch or go get it instead of passing the ball to me like a normal fan would do, and so yeah, so then I rolled him a middle finger in return.".

    Sources indicate that philadelphia's fans aren't known for being especially kind to opposing players, and George's tenure in Philadelphia didn't exactly go as planned. After signing a four-year max contract in the summer of 2024, George, due to a combination of injuries and a suspension, played just 78 regular-season games for the 76ers. Most of that time was spent playing below his typical standard, though he thrived after returning from that 25-game suspension a year ago and wound up being vital in Philadelphia's first-round comeback against Boston.

    Now that George is thriving for a rival, there was seemingly some bitterness in the crowd. And George made it perfectly clear how he felt about that both during the game and after it.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, to no one's real surprise, Jacob Misiorowski of the Milwaukee Brewers and Cam Schlittler of the New York Yankees have been named the 2026 Cy Young Award winners for, respectively, the National League and American League.
    • Obviously, Cy Young winners have necessarily authored excellent seasons, but in the case of this year's winners, the descriptor "excellent" doesn't quite rise to meet the work of Misiorowski and Schlittler:.
    • Recent findings suggest that we could get into stuff, yes, as each has a blazing fastball that overwhelms hitters at the front end of a deep repertoire.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, to no one's real surprise, Jacob Misiorowski of the Milwaukee Brewers and Cam Schlittler of the New York Yankees have been named the 2026 Cy Young Award winners for, respectively, the National League and American League. Each was announced as the winner of Major League Baseball's topmost honor for pitchers, and each won the balloting in unanimous fashion. They are the first duo to win unanimously in the same year in their respective leagues since Justin Verlander and Sandy Alcantara in 2022 and just the third in MLB history.

    Obviously, Cy Young winners have necessarily authored excellent seasons, but in the case of this year's winners, the descriptor "excellent" doesn't quite rise to meet the work of Misiorowski and Schlittler:.

    Recent findings suggest that we could get into stuff, yes, as each has a blazing fastball that overwhelms hitters at the front end of a deep repertoire. This exercise, though, is more about how Misiorowski and Schlittler have overwhelmed the opposition when it comes to keeping runs off the board. You'll note all the strikeouts above, of course, but what may catch the eye is that each boasts a sub-2.00 ERA. That's a time-honored signifier of pitcher impeccability, even if ERA has its flaws.

    To upgrade this familiar stat just a bit – and to put the two 2026 Cy Young winners' accomplishments into fitting context – we'll turn to ERA+. ERA+ is ERA adjusted to reflect league and home ballpark tendencies. An ERA+ of 100 represents the league average, and each point above or below that mark reflects a one-point change. For example, a pitcher with an ERA+ of 120 had a park- and league-adjusted ERA that was 20% better than the league average, while a pitcher with an ERA+ of 95 was 5% worse than the league average. So from the hurlers' standpoint, the higher the ERA+, the better.

    Industry observers note that this is all a necessary step when comparing pitchers across eras, because run–scoring environments have changed so drastically over the history of the sport. For example, Pedro Martinez's ERA of 1.74 in 2000, when teams were averaging more than five runs per game, means a lot more than, say, Charlie Chech's 1.74 ERA in 1908, when teams averaged 3.38 runs per game. That's where ERA+ comes in. Martinez in 2000 had an ERA+ of 291, or a park-adjusted ERA that was 191% (!) better than the league average. Chech in 1908 had the same ERA as Martinez in 2000, but his ERA+ of 136 was drastically worse.

    According to recent reports, as for the two moundsmen of present interest, Misiorowski this past season had an ERA+ of 232, which led the majors. Schlittler had an ERA+ of 215, which led the American League. Yes, they had those sub-2.00 ERAs, but, really, topping a 200 ERA+ is a much more impressive achievement. Counting Misiorowski and Schlittler but throwing out the pitchers who achieved the mark in the 60-game 2020 season (you should always throw out 2020), just 43 pitchers in MLB since 1900 have managed a 200 ERA+ or better across a qualifying number of innings. Over that same span and with 2020 also omitted, 201 pitchers have achieved a sub-2.00 ERA in a qualifying number of innings.

    It has been revealed that as you can imagine, it's a rarity to have not one but two pitchers in the same season who have a 200 ERA+ or better, as was the case this past season with Misiorowski and Schlittler. How rare? No season has ever given us more than two such qualifiers. Here's the full list of those across all of modern MLB history (i.e., since 1900):.

    Jacob Misiorowski, Brewers (232); Cam Schlittler, Yankees (215).

    Jacob deGrom, Mets (218); Blake Snell, Rays (217).

    Jake Arrieta, Cubs (215), Zack Greinke, Dodgers (222).

    Roger Clemens, Blue Jays (222); Pedro Martinez, Expos (219).

    Carl Lundgren, Cubs (211); Jack Pfiester, Cubs (214).

    Christy Mathewson, Giants (233); Ed Reulbach, Cubs (209).

    Yes, just six seasons have given us more than one 200 ERA+ pitcher, and this year's Miz-Cam combo marks just the third time that we've had one from each league. Accordingly, this marks just the third time that each Cy Young winner has reached the 200 ERA+ benchmark in a given season.

    There's another, even more exclusive group that puts the Miz-Cam tandem in the proper context and hints at a future that's as bright as their present and their recent past. In 2026, Schlittler was in his age-25 campaign, while Misiorowski was in his age-24 season. So they're young as frontline aces go, and while you never want to make assumptions about pitcher health and durability in the current era, this duo's elite performance at both top-line and underlying level raises the possibility that each will win another Cy or two (or three) in the years to come.

    Recent findings suggest that turning back to the 200 ERA+ defining stat, such youth in tandem with such excellence is all but unprecedented. Of the seasons listed just above, just 1905 featured two pitchers who, like Miz and Cam this past season, were age 25 or younger at the time. Mathewson, the inner-circle all-time great, was 24 that season and Reulbach was a 22-year-old rookie. We haven't seen something like that in more than 120 years.

    Industry observers note that let's also note that Misiorowski and Shlittler, who each struck out more than 30% of opposing batters this season, absolutely have the stuff and foundational, forward-looking results to continue lording over their guild. Until that comes to pass, though, let's appreciate ther historical rare success and their even more historically rare combination of success and youth.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that the Fresh England Patriots may have to finish the 2026 season without their franchise centerpiece.
    • According to recent reports, maye suffered the injury on the final offensive snap of Newly introduced England's opening drive against the Detroit Lions during their Week 10 matchup in Munich, Germany.
    • Immediately after the game, coach Mike Vrabel didn't have much of an upgrade on Maye's status.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that the Fresh England Patriots may have to finish the 2026 season without their franchise centerpiece. Quarterback Drake Maye is believed to have suffered a significant lower-leg injury that is poised to sideline him for an extended period of time, according ESPN. The report notes that the injury has the potential to keep Maye out for the remainder of the year. Specifically, ESPN reports that the team fears Maye fractured his ankle.

    According to recent reports, maye suffered the injury on the final offensive snap of Newly introduced England's opening drive against the Detroit Lions during their Week 10 matchup in Munich, Germany. The third-year quarterback was sacked by pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson on a third-and-goal play and was in noticeable discomfort after the hit. After being looked at on the sideline, Maye gingerly walked to the locker room where he was eventually ruled out with what the team called an ankle injury.

    Immediately after the game, coach Mike Vrabel didn't have much of an upgrade on Maye's status. However, Vrabel told WEEI's "The Greg Hill Show" on Monday morning that Maye stayed back in Germany.

    Recent findings suggest that "The patch that I have is just out of caution, Drake stayed back,' Vrabel noted, via the Boston Herald. "He'll be traveling back here shortly. But just wanted to make sure that everything was good for him to travel back and safely. The things that go around injuries, and just wanted to make sure everything was in line for him to travel, and it seems like he is. He'll be returning here, I think, shortly.".

    In a recent development, given that Maye was unable to travel back with the team following the international contest, this lends credence to this latest report on the severity of the injury. ESPN's report highlights that Maye stayed in Germany to undergo additional tests to determine whether he needs surgery.

    Recent findings suggest that maye -- along with the entire Patriots team -- has come back down to earth a bit in 2026 following his MVP runner-up season last year as Latest England made a surprise Super Bowl run. Through 10 games, Maye was 5-5 as the starter, completed 65.6% of his passes, averaged 233.0 passing yards per game, and threw for 18 touchdowns. He's also thrown 11 interceptions, which are already a career high.

    Of course, it's never a good time for your franchise quarterback to endure a potential season-ending injury, but Maye going down comes at a critical juncture of New England's season. The club is reeling after losing three of its last four games, dropping it back to .500 on the season.

    Sources indicate that this latest loss to Detroit pushes them further behind the Buffalo Bills (8-1) in the AFC East race, and they are now on the outside looking in on the AFC playoff picture. Coming into Week 10, they were slotted as the No. 7 seed, but are now sitting as the No. 8 seed and looking up to the Cleveland Browns (6-4), Pittsburgh Steelers (6-3), and Denver Broncos (7-2) for the three wild card spots.

    Recent findings suggest that the Patriots will have the bye to collect themselves in Week 11, but the road ahead doesn't get any easier, particularly in December, when they'll face the Bills, Vikings, and Chiefs (road) over a three-week span. Not having Maye for those matchups would make Fresh England significant underdogs, even with two of those games at Gillette Stadium.

    Industry observers note that with Maye on the shelf, the Patriots will first turn to top backup Tommy DeVito. He stepped in during their contest with Detroit in Germany on Sunday. In that game, DeVito put up less-than-stellar numbers, completing 12-of-24 for 81 yards, a touchdown and an interception. He also rushed four times for 19 yards on the ground.

    DeVito has been with Fresh England for the past two seasons after being claimed off waivers in August of 2025 following his release from the New York Giants. Last offseason, he signed a two-year, $7.4 million extension with the team and became the primary back to Maye entering 2026.

    The 28-year-old has starting experience, having logged eight starts over his career since entering the NFL in 2023 as an undrafted free agent out of Illinois. DeVito is 3-5 over those starts and has a 63.4% completion percentage to go along with an 84.6 passer rating for his career.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It's hard to imagine a better start for the Lakers.
    • It has been revealed that so far, Dončić ranks first in steals (20), first in defensive loose balls recovered (9) and second in charges drawn (4).
    • Dončić isn't just in the right place at the right time for a steal; his foul rate is down on contests, and scorers are shooting just 25% on 2-pointers when he's the closest defender, some 30% worse than their expected conversion rate from that spot, per NBA.com tracking.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It's hard to imagine a better start for the Lakers. They are 10-2 and shooting the lights out as Luka Dončić pilots the league's top-ranked offense. Dončić's historic numbers speak for themselves, but he's doing more than getting and creating buckets. You've likely seen his defensive metrics making the social-media rounds, and they're legitimate. He's in great shape, and the multiple-effort energy is showing up, frankly, more on the defenisve end than on offense, where he's always a monster.

    It has been revealed that so far, Dončić ranks first in steals (20), first in defensive loose balls recovered (9) and second in charges drawn (4). It's key to point out that Luka has always been a fairly productive box-score defender, certainly beyond what one of the worst defensive reputations in NBA history would suggest, but this year it looks different. His stop rate of 4.2 (meaning he finishes 4.2 of every 100 possessions with either a steal or a drawn offensive foul), per Databallr, ranks higher than many others, including the likes of Jaden McDaniels and Ausar Thompson.

    Dončić isn't just in the right place at the right time for a steal; his foul rate is down on contests, and scorers are shooting just 25% on 2-pointers when he's the closest defender, some 30% worse than their expected conversion rate from that spot, per NBA.com tracking.

    Include the 3-pointers he's contesting, opponents are shooting 32.3% against Luka -- 13% worse than expected. To put that number in perspective, it's second only to Victor Wembanyama among players who've defended at least 40 shots.

    As usual, offenses are hunting Dončić, who is facing an isolation on 17.5% of his defensive possessions (a 95th-percentile frequency), per Synergy, but he's only surrendering 0.79 points per possession on those isos (his man is 8 for 22), which is a 71st percentile ranking.

    Sources indicate that it's worth repeating, as is the case with his steals (even though he's on a career-high pace here) and deflections, Dončić has long had better defensive metrics than his reputation would suggest. Dating back to his last year in Dallas, his defensive iso numbers are roughly average, and he's averaged almost a steal and a half per game for his career.

    Recent findings suggest that the difference this season is in the movement (better shape), the multiple efforts, the ability to genuinely stay in front without fouling more times than not. He's a real part of a Lakers defense that is eight points per 100 better with him on the floor and, overall, is giving up nearly three fewer points per 100 than it did last season.

    Throw in Luka's red-hot shooting/scoring start, the All-NBA track that Austin Reaves is on, Walker Kessler's combination of rim protection, lob-partner chemistry with Dončić and offensive rebounding and the Lakers, though not a perfect team (they turn it over a lot and need to rebound better defensively), continue to look like a top-five team in the early going.

    In fact, the Lakers are a top-two team this week. And with that, on to this week's Power Rankings.

Travel hiccups were much more defined in the college game and impacted countless games, some of which were delayed multiple hours to accommodate teams' late arrivals.

    Of the 14 highest-profile games that featured programs which experienced travel complications, those teams went 9-5, so it's hard to say the flight disruptions were to blame for any poor play.

    The biggest snag came in the matchup between Ole Miss and Oklahoma. A handful of challenges including a timed-out flight crew and a small airport left the Rebels grounded until Saturday and led the SEC to push the game to Sunday.

    The conference's decision was highly unpopular among Oklahoma stakeholders. Sooners athletic director Roger Denny put the league on blast for forcing his program to comply with the schedule change. Legendary former Sooners coach Bob Stoops chimed in with his own criticism of commissioner Greg Sankey.

    In the end, the Sooners pulled off a 24-17 win anyway. Their revitalized offense controlled the game flow in a victory over a ranked opponent and provided proof of concept that Jason Witten could be the answer as the team's potential full-time offensive coordinator. Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott even said Witten could be an NFL coach.

    LSU's last chance to secure a resume-building win was dashed by Texas. The Tigers led by as many as 11 points in a marquee matchup and were two seconds away from closing it out when Arch Manning connected with Raleek Brown on a game-winning swing pass for the Longhorns. From the Tigers' standpoint, it was the most devastating loss for a CFP bubble team in Week 11 and another stain on Lane Kiffin's young tenure. He was the biggest individual loser of the week.

    Recent findings suggest that manning's heroics came in another clutch moment for college football's most polarizing quarterback, who relished in the fact that his team dealt the decisive blow to LSU's playoff hopes. On the opposing sideline, Kiffin watched his championship expectations come crumbling down in that moment. Our Chris Hummer was on site to tell the story.

    Sources indicate that in the Substantial Ten, Indiana has a quarterback controversy. Seventh-year senior Grant Wilson might just be the key to the Hoosiers' search for a second consecutive national championship, not Josh Hoover, the expensive transfer they brought in to lead them back to glory. Wilson guided Indiana to a 27-13 win over USC and left Lincoln Riley to tell the same old story to Trojans fans.

    In the ACC, Miami turned in a "B" performance in its second game without Malachi Toney, and Wake Forest obliterated SMU in a statement game.

    Sources indicate that week 11 also dialed up the heat on the hot seat. For now, the pressure is off Deion Sanders. He orchestrated Colorado's first top-15 win since 2007 in a stunner against Houston. Dabo Swinney, on the other hand, reached a newly introduced low. Clemson has now lost nine of its last 11 home games against Power Four opponents.

    Jazz's nightmare season continues with Lauri Markkanen set to miss at least a month

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that another day, another misfortune for the Utah Jazz.
    • Markkanen's absence will leave the Jazz even further shorthanded in the front court, where they are already running out of bodies.
    • Meanwhile, the Jazz could have had a far deeper and younger frontcourt had they simply made different decisions in the offseason.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that another day, another misfortune for the Utah Jazz. After a four-year rebuild that included tanking so egregiously that they were punished for it on multiple occasions, the Jazz expected to compete for a playoff spot this season after winning the No. 2 pick in the 2026 NBA Draft. Instead, they are an NBA-worst 1-10, and things just got worse as All-Star forward Lauri Markkanen will miss at least a month after suffering two nondisplaced fractures in his right hand.

    Markkanen's absence will leave the Jazz even further shorthanded in the front court, where they are already running out of bodies. Last season's major-name deadline acquisition, Jaren Jackson Jr., was already out with a torn MCL, which has a 6-8-week recovery timeline. Additionally, starting center Jusuf Nurkić hasn't played this season due to a toe injury sustained in the preseason.

    Meanwhile, the Jazz could have had a far deeper and younger frontcourt had they simply made different decisions in the offseason. They elected to sign-and-trade starting center Walker Kessler to the Los Angeles Lakers for a haul of draft picks that may one day prove valuable, but won't ease fan frustration in watching Kessler thrive as a cornerstone of a Lakers team with the NBA's best record at 10-2. They passed on power forward Cameron Boozer with the No. 2 overall pick despite the presence of his father, former Jazz All-Star Carlos Boozer, in their scouting department. Now Boozer has the second-best Rookie of the Year odds for the Memphis Grizzlies, who are 7-3.

    These decisions may eventually bear fruit. No. 2 pick Darryn Peterson is starting to figure things out after a terrible start, averaging 24 points in his last three outings, all of which have come against strong defenses. The Jazz will presumably seek a cheaper Kessler replacement eventually, and the draft surplus generated by trading him is going to be important once Utah's young core starts to get expensive.

    But the Jazz have been selling long-term outlook since they traded Rudy Gobert and Donovan Mitchell four summers ago. Their two former stars have been playoff mainstays elsewhere. Kessler and Boozer both figure to be as well. Nobody expected the Jazz to win the 2027 championship, but at a certain point, promise has to become progress.

    These front-court injuries put any hope of short-term progress on hold, and Utah doesn't even stand to benefit from these struggles because its 2027 first-round pick belongs to the Grizzlies. The Jazz were already having perhaps the NBA's bleakest start, and losing Markkanen now might be the tipping point towards yet another lost season.
