    Two days after losing by 51 points to the Golden State Warriors, the New Orleans Pelicans managed an even more embarrassing loss on Wednesday when they were blown out 145-111 by the Brooklyn Nets, who were 2-8 entering the night.

    Recent findings suggest that new Orleans (4-8) began the season on a four-game losing streak before bouncing back to .500 with a four-game winning streak, but has now lost four straight again. The concerning part of their recent skid is that the Pelicans have grown increasingly uncompetitive.

    Industry observers note that in that initial four-game losing streak to open the season, the Pelicans lost by a combined 23 points in the four games. In their last two games, they've lost by a combined 85 points, leaving Zion Williamson with just one word to describe his team's effort.

    "Unacceptable," Williamson said, via ESPN. "I don't even have a lot of words. Just unacceptable.".

    Recent findings suggest that williamson called out the Pelicans' defensive effort during this latest losing streak, as they've allowed at least 138 points in three consecutive games. The seventh-year star then called for his team to look inward and be honest with themselves about whether they're doing everything they can to help the team win.

    "I said nobody likes to lose like this, but if we don't like to lose like this, we have to start with ourselves first," Williamson said. "Look in the mirror and say, did I do what I needed to do for my team? Not individually. Did I do what I needed to do for my team? And then we go from there.".

    In a recent development, it's never a good sign when a team's star is questioning the collective's effort level and commitment to winning just 12 games into the season. This is when buy-in should be the easiest to get because a team's goals are still right in front of them, but the Pelicans are already showing signs that they will likely spend another season at the bottom of the Western Conference.

    That four-game winning streak -- which was somewhat schedule-aided with two games against the woeful Sacramento Kings and Utah Jazz -- feels like ages ago for the Pelicans. If they're going to turn things around, Williamson is right that it starts with accountability from the players, but with some key injuries to Trey Murphy III and Yves Missi, coupled with poor play, this season could get away from Latest Orleans swiftly.

    Joe Burrow isn't just chasing MVP, he's chasing the greatest passing season ever

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (854 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Two years ago, Joe Burrow resigned himself to the fact that, despite having an MVP-caliber season, he likely wouldn't win the award based on the Bengals' 9-8 record and absence from the playoffs.
    • Industry observers note that already the MVP favorite entering Sunday night's game against the Steelers, Burrow is now the clear front-runner.
    • Playing in the background of Burrow's performance were MVP chants from Bengals fans, which Taylor acknowledged hearing throughout the game.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Two years ago, Joe Burrow resigned himself to the fact that, despite having an MVP-caliber season, he likely wouldn't win the award based on the Bengals' 9-8 record and absence from the playoffs.

    "I'll win one one day," Burrow said at the time.

    That time could very well be now.

    Industry observers note that already the MVP favorite entering Sunday night's game against the Steelers, Burrow is now the clear front-runner. Against a team that defeated the Bengals back in Week 3, Burrow threw for 409 yards and four touchdowns while completing nearly 80% of his passes. It could have been much more, but Bengals coach Zac Taylor called off the dogs and took Burrow out of the game midway through the fourth quarter of Cincinnati's eventual 38-18 win.

    Playing in the background of Burrow's performance were MVP chants from Bengals fans, which Taylor acknowledged hearing throughout the game. Taylor, as you'd expect, agrees with that sentiment.

    In a recent development, "I mean it would be impossible to say that anyone is playing better," Taylor mentioned. "I'm not watching every game ... but I bet the people that aren't talking about him aren't watching our games, because if you are, it's really hard to say that he is not the best player on planet Earth.".

    Burrow's performance not only strengthened his MVP case but also put him on a historic trajectory with eight games to play in the 2026 regular season.

    Burrow is one of only five quarterbacks in NFL history with over 30 total touchdowns through nine games, according to CBS Sports Research. The other four won league MVP: Tom Brady in 2007, Aaron Rodgers in 2011, Peyton Manning in 2013 and Patrick Mahomes in 2018.

    Sources indicate that burrow joined Manning on Sunday night as the only two quarterbacks with five consecutive games with at least four touchdowns. Over that span, Burrow has thrown 20 touchdowns (against just three interceptions) and ran for two more while completing 78% of his passes. The Bengals won each of those games while taking sole possession of first place in the AFC North.

    Burrow is on pace to become the third quarterback to throw for 5,000 yards and 50 touchdowns in a season. He is on pace to throw 51 touchdown passes, which would put him behind Manning's 55 during the 2013 season. Burrow's 5,279 yards would rank fourth behind Manning (5,477 in 2013), Drew Brees (5,476 in 2011) and Brady (5,316 in 2021).

    Sources indicate that while he's not on pace to break those records, Burrow is on track to create his own category for quarterback excellence by becoming the first quarterback to throw for 5,000 yards and 50 touchdowns in a season while also completing 70% of his passes. If he does that, he will have a strong argument when it comes to having the greatest passing season in league history.

    It has been revealed that burrow's success can be attributed to his growth as well as improvements across Cincinnati's entire roster. The Bengals' offensive line has improved, and the defense has greatly benefited from the offseason acquisitions of Dexter Lawrence, Boye Mafe and Bryan Cook. It goes without saying that the trio of running back Chase Brown and wideouts Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have helped, too.

    According to recent reports, now in his fourth season, Brown has established himself as one of the league's more versatile running backs. He had two touchdown catches on Sunday night and was second on the team with eight receptions.

    "We know what we have in Chase," Burrow stated. "He's a significant-time playmaker for us. When people devote too many resources to stopping the guys on the outside, Chase can beat you in a lot of different ways.".

    That's now two TDs for Chase Brown and FOUR TDs for Joe Burrow 😎PITvsCIN on NBC/PeacockStream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/svZHSPGVmC.

    Chase and Higgins are the league's best receiving duo and have been for some time. They're on pace to become the first pair of teammates to each post 1,500-yard receiving seasons in the same year.

    Higgins is on pace to record a career-high 1,556 receiving yards this season, while Chase (who actually trailed Higgins in receiving yards prior to Sunday night) is on pace to have 1,658 receiving yards this season after catching 11 passes for 231 yards against Pittsburgh.

    Joe Burrow throws it deep to Ja'Marr Chase for the first down 🚀PITvsCIN on NBC/PeacockStream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/o97edw3OV3.

    It has been revealed that looking ahead, the Bengals have only three remaining games against teams with winning records (Cleveland in Weeks 13 and 18, the Chiefs in Week 14). The Browns have given Burrow fits in the past, but Myles Garrett (now a Ram) was a significant reason for that. Burrow has historically played well against the Chiefs.

    As Burrow alluded to in his postgame press conference, it's only mid-November with a lot of football left to play. That may be true, but it is also true that Burrow has put himself -- and his team -- in position to have a memorable, and perhaps historic, season.

    Stephen Curry injury: Warriors star to miss at least two weeks with oblique tear amid Golden State's hot start

    📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (550 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Golden State Warriors' fairytale start to the season got a dose of reality on Wednesday when Stephen Curry suffered an injury to his oblique in a loss to the Houston Rockets.
    • According to recent reports, an MRI on Thursday confirmed an oblique abdominal tear and the team announced that Curry will be re-evaluated in two weeks.
    • The injury happened halfway through the first quarter.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Golden State Warriors' fairytale start to the season got a dose of reality on Wednesday when Stephen Curry suffered an injury to his oblique in a loss to the Houston Rockets.

    According to recent reports, an MRI on Thursday confirmed an oblique abdominal tear and the team announced that Curry will be re-evaluated in two weeks. While two weeks is the best-case scenario, that being just the re-evaluation point means his absence could extend beyond that timetable -- as that also doesn't include any ramp-up process he would need to clear before returning to the floor.

    The injury happened halfway through the first quarter. You can see Curry get tangled up with Alperen Sengun and grab at his side after they separate.

    Steph Curry got injured after Sengun grabbed and twisted his arm pic.twitter.com/4p20Rogpeu.

    Moments later, Curry hit his lone 3-pointer of the game and could once again be seen grabbing at his side after the shot.

    In a recent development, stephen Curry headed to the locker room with an apparent right hip injury. pic.twitter.com/1zVrNz00bH.

    According to recent reports, curry exited the game at the next dead ball and didn't return. After the game, Warriors coach Steve Kerr said concern about Curry's injury was "high.".

    Sources indicate that "He noted he tweaked something in his abdominal area," Kerr said. "He said he's never done it before. ... Concern is high, but I have no idea the extent of the injury.".

    In recent seasons, the range of recovery times for other notable NBA oblique injuries has varied.

    It's unclear how severe Curry's oblique tear is. These are all strains, which is code for a minor tear, but the worst-case scenario would be a more severe one. We saw this two years ago when the Orlando Magic lost both Franz Wagner and Paolo Banchero to oblique tears that kept Banchero out for 10 weeks and Wagner for more than a month.

    In a recent development, any extended absence would be disastrous for the Warriors, who are not equipped to cover for any Curry injury. Curry has gotten off to a scorching start, entering Wednesday averaging 30.1 points per game on 50.3/45.7/98.7 shooting splits with Golden State winning eight straight games for the first time since the 2022 championship season.

    But this was always a fingers-crossed situation with an aging roster. Already down Jimmy Butler and Kristaps Porziņģis, and with Brandon Williams and Gary Payton II also on the shelf and wing Will Richard playing through a ligament tear in his thumb, the Warriors have little, if any, margin for any more injuries.

    This comes at a particularly tough time for the Warriors, who are entering their most difficult stretch of the season. On Friday, they'll visit the San Antonio Spurs before facing the Dallas Mavericks and New Orleans Pelicans on a back-to-back.

    The Warriors have opened up at 8-4 with a top-three offense, but that can go south very promptly without Curry.

    Curry is the latest NBA star to face an extended injury absence in the first month of the 2026-27 season. Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren (Thunder), Anthony Edwards (Timberwolves), Tyrese Haliburton (Pacers), Kawhi Leonard (Raptors), Paolo Banchero (Magic), Jalen Duren (Pistons) and Kon Knueppel (Hornets) are among the players right now dealing with multi-week absences.

    Latest Update: Sean Payton disputes Jim Harbaugh's 'loophole' claim after Broncos-Chargers trade falls apart

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (409 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that at the trade deadline last Tuesday, a rare inter-division deal was agreed to between the Los Angeles Chargers and Denver Broncos.
    • It has been revealed that the trade was nixed after Denver reportedly found an concern with Henley's knee during his physical.
    • Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters last Thursday that the Broncos backing out of the deal sets a bad precedent, and that this is a "loophole" the NFL needs to investigate.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that at the trade deadline last Tuesday, a rare inter-division deal was agreed to between the Los Angeles Chargers and Denver Broncos. The Broncos agreed to send the Chargers a fourth-round pick and a future fifth-round pick in exchange for linebacker Daiyan Henley, but the deal fell apart.

    It has been revealed that the trade was nixed after Denver reportedly found an concern with Henley's knee during his physical. ESPN reported that the Broncos then approached the Chargers and attempted to renegotiate the compensation. Denver still wanted to acquire the linebacker, but just not at the price George Paton and Sean Payton initially agreed to.

    Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters last Thursday that the Broncos backing out of the deal sets a bad precedent, and that this is a "loophole" the NFL needs to investigate.

    It has been revealed that "That's why it's a loophole, and teams should not have the ability to do that," Harbaugh stated. "It's a medical grade. It's a pass/fail for a medical trade. They told us they weren't going to pass him if there was a fourth and a fifth, which was agreed upon. They would not pass him for that. They would pass him for a fourth and a 'fill in the blank.' I don't know what to call that, but that's what it is.".

    The Broncos were on a bye in Week 10, so we had to wait until Monday to hear their side of the story. Payton was indeed asked about the trade falling through, but didn't offer many details.

    "I'm not going to get into the specifics. He's prospect we thought of — and still do — very highly of. It just didn't work out," Payton said, via The Athletic. "I'll leave it at that.".

    What did Payton think about Harbaugh's comments regarding a "loophole?".

    It has been revealed that "Listen, I thought I saw it all," he stated, via Mile High Sports. "There's no loophole. It's just part of the trade process, every step of the way.".

    Whatever the Broncos found in Henley's knee hasn't affected him yet. He hasn't missed a game due to injury in each of the last two seasons. In eight games played this season, Henley has recorded 51 tackles, half a sack, two passes defensed and an interception. The Broncos and Chargers will see each other again in the regular-season finale when Week 18 rolls around.
